Mechanically discovers the available sidecar panel, recruits at least one cross-family verifier when present, and degrades gracefully when none are. The governor (Claude) keeps the terminal verdict; sidecar findings must be source-grounded before acceptance. Opt-in via one-time consent, stored in the UAP; fires only on load-bearing changes. Triggered by "recruit a cross-family check", "decorrelate this verification", "use the idle sidecars to verify", "auto-decorrelation".

name: contention-layer
description: When two skills, agents, or independent research tracks produce conflicting verdicts on the same output, reads the conflict as a signal rather than an error and harvests new skill candidates or insight deltas — including a Dual-Track Grounding conflict (open-frontier track vs internally-grounded recall track disagreeing). Routes skills born from contention to fh-meta (meta-layer), the commons plugin (project-agnostic), or field harvest (domain-specific). Triggered by "two skills conflict", "they produce different conclusions", "contention-layer", "contention harvest", "open vs grounded contradiction", "research tracks disagree".

name: context-doctor
description: Reduces token waste in Claude Code sessions (run the built-in `/context` first; this skill covers what it does not) across two axes — context footprint (auto-generates .claudeignore, guides over-read files and /clear timing) and command output (routes to a command-output proxy/hook such as rtk to trim verbose CLI stdout). In hub environments, regularly audits bloated CLAUDE.md/MEMORY.md/memory/*.md files and proposes compression. Usable standalone without a hub clone.

name: corpus-grounding-expander
description: Fetches and normalizes multi-version public-domain corpora into a single verified-axiom store for verbatim-relay grounding, recording per-version license and provenance.

name: cross-ecosystem-synergy-detection
description: Automatically discovers useful combinations (synergy pairs) across multiple installed plugins and skills, and presents them as a ranked table. Proactively suggests undiscovered synergies when new projects or skills are registered in the registry. Activates on phrases like "do my installed tools work well together?", "they seem to work in isolation", "find synergies".

name: deep-clarify
description: Clarifies ambiguous requests through Socratic dialogue, drawing out goals, completion criteria, and constraints to produce a structured spec document. Pre-dispatch requirement clarification step for agent dispatch. Triggered by "I don't know what to build", "how should I approach this", "organize this for me", "clarify this", "deep-clarify".

name: dialogue-harvest
description: Mines improvement insights from long-form AI dialogue logs and long texts — an external or pasted corpus, not the current session (current-session wrap-up belongs to harvest-loop). First operation is sycophancy removal — separates speakers, strips the counterpart's agreement/restatement spans, converts the user's own utterances into falsifiable propositions, and labels each proposition induced (frame first introduced by the counterpart) or independent (originated with the user). Ships a drop counter so removed material is visible, never silently lost. Triggered by "mine insights from this chat log", "이 대화록에서 통찰 캐줘", "strip the agreement and show me what's actually mine", "동조 걷어내고 알맹이만", "what did I actually contribute in this thread".

name: edit-manifest
description: Implements a predict-verify loop for harness edits. Every SKILL.md, rules/*.md, or CLAUDE.md change is paired with a predicted impact stored in a manifest. The next session verifies predictions against actual outcomes, and a validation gate accepts edits only when improvement is measurable. Runs automatically on harvest-loop Step 0-c and on explicit invocation.

name: fh
description: Renders the FH hub map on demand — the door menu, a starter set of skills, and the most-used trigger phrases — without requiring a greeting. State-aware; composes live candidates from the session card and tracks.

name: field-harvest
description: Scans git history of field projects to detect patterns worth backporting to the meta-harness (Mode A), and logs session work to the knowledge hub when a session ends (Mode B). Triggers on "save this pattern", "make this reusable across projects", "can we automate this repetition?", "push this to FH", "reverse absorption", "harvest pattern", "session log", "log today's work", "sync to hub".

name: frontier-digest
description: Collects the latest AI/harness engineering trends from HackerNews, arxiv, launch channels (Launch YC, Product Hunt, Show HN), GeekNews and vendor changelogs, then synthesizes them into actionable insights directly relevant to forge-harness operations. Triggered by "AI trends", "latest trends", "this week's AI updates", "what's on the frontier", "harness trends", "frontier-digest".

name: goal-quench
description: Wraps /goal with a tiered safety + orchestration ladder. core (default): a token budget gate (pre-run estimate), mid-run budget thresholds, and an automatic post-run quality verification via pipeline-conductor — closing /goal's two gaps (the runner's per-turn judge evaluates completion, pipeline-conductor evaluates correctness). pro: adds context-doctor token reduction and agent-composer goal decomposition. max: adds internal-first capability-gap fill (LOCAL_SKILL_REGISTRY skill-bus scan → plugin-recommender external search → auto_project_mapping map/cluster) and cross-ecosystem-synergy-detection pre-validation. The Phase-1 budget verdict auto-recommends the mode. Triggered by "goal with quality gate", "safe goal", "goal-quench", "orchestrate this goal", or before running /goal on high-stakes tasks.

name: harness-doctor
description: Scans a project's harness structure (.claude/ directory, CLAUDE.md, rules, agents) to diagnose complexity, drift, missing files, and broken references, then suggests improvements. `--lint` flag adds language-pattern scan (self-marketing, cushion words, version brags). Triggered by "harness check", "structure diagnosis", "CLAUDE.md audit".

name: harness-pr-reviewer
description: Checks a submitted PR against the environment's baseline assets (CLAUDE.md, memory, naming, asset classification) and attaches a review comment with a merge recommendation. 5 steps — diff read, 8-area consistency check, self-catch, comment, merge recommendation.

name: harvest-loop
description: An 8-step self-evolution pipeline that runs after field sessions end (field-harvest → contention-layer → challenger + persona-innovator → synthesizer → Critic agent → harness-doctor → verify-bidirectional → curator), absorbing session learnings back into the FH ecosystem. Runs automatically at session end in the main dev environment; proposes execution first for external users. Triggered by "session harvest", "learning absorption", "fh evolution", or "harvest-loop". (The phrase "run the pipeline" is ceded to pipeline-conductor — use that for end-to-end verification sweeps.)

name: install-doctor
description: Scans the existing environment (after the built-in `/doctor` — this covers FH-plugin conflicts it does not) before and after meta-harness plugin install to diagnose conflicts, duplicates, and silent overwrite risks. Reports potential conflict areas with existing CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, and audit practices. Activates on "install conflict", "any overlaps?", "is it safe to install?".

name: install-wizard
description: Run when setting up a new project for the first time or onboarding after installing FH (first setup, initial configuration, onboarding start, configure project, help me set up). Performs environment detection → gap diagnosis → item-by-item suggestions → user approval → execution → acceleration baseline setup in sequence. Use --dry-run to output diagnosis report only (bg dispatch compatible).

name: marketplace-gate
description: Evaluates whether a repository meets marketplace listing criteria via a 5-point check and outputs a listing suitability verdict. Checks README completeness, zero-config readiness, maintenance signals, duplication, and public safety.

name: memory-hygiene
description: Detects "stale-but-confident" memory entries — facts that were once verified but have silently drifted. Scans memory/*.md for entries past their staleness threshold and proposes re-verification or archival. Runs automatically as part of harvest-loop Step 0-c and on explicit invocation.

name: meta-prompt-builder
description: Generates structured prompts to send to each agent in an agent dispatch plan. Triggered by "write the instructions", "what do I say to the agent?", "write the prompt for me", "meta-prompt-builder". Bridges agent-composer (which agents) and prompt content (what to say). Uses Goal/Context/Constraints/Done When structure.

name: persona-roster-expander
description: Expands a named persona seed into a tiered, judgment-mapped cast — tiering each persona by a domain safety rule, mapping each to a decision-lens in the user's vocabulary, then proposing additional voices with sourced anchors.

name: phantom-quench
description: Input-tracing grounding audit for artifacts such as test cases, analysis reports, and design docs. Extracts proper nouns, numbers, citations, version claims, and branching conditions, then back-traces each to declared local files by grep or to external sources by fetch-and-support checks. Marks missing anchors as Phantom Claims and cited-but-unsupporting anchors as Unsupported. A claim is grounded only by non-model evidence: a local hit or literal source span, never another model's agreement. Renamed from source-grounding-audit; old-name references still route here. Triggered by: "phantom detection", "phantom claim", "source back-trace", "where did this come from", "verify source", "does the source support this claim", "grounding audit", "source grounding audit", "citation support check".

name: pipeline-conductor
description: Chains the four core FH verification pipelines (harvest-loop → steel-quench → phantom-quench → sim-conductor) into a single gated sweep. Accepts a scope (single skill, specific asset, full harness) and aggregates results into one structured report. Supports --quick mode (steps 2+3 only) and --full mode (all four steps). Triggered by "run the full pipeline", "chain all verifications", "end-to-end sweep", "pipeline-conductor", or "verify everything".

name: plugin-recommender
description: Given a task description, searches internal and external open-source ecosystems (including Codex marketplace and Claude Code marketplace) to find and recommend suitable plugins with installation guidance. Recommendation is quality-validation based (marketplace-listed + performance-validated), not source-origin based. Activates on "recommend a plugin", "what tool should I use?", "is there a plugin for this?", "recommend a tool". Also checks for duplicate installations.

name: prompt-regression
description: Statically checks harness assets against a known-answer probe set after rule/skill changes — inspects the changed source for the trigger phrases, chain links and gate conditions each probe expects, and reports PASS/FAIL/SKIP per probe. Source inspection only; it does not run live sessions, so it catches assets that no longer SAY the right thing, not models that stop DOING it. Triggers on "prompt regression", "did my changes break anything", "regression check", "test harness changes".

name: public-surface-audit
description: Scans git-tracked (public) files for operator-private tokens that should live only in gitignored files — real usernames, absolute home paths, companion-store names, company asset names. Reports file:line + matched token + severity, so a public/private split stays clean before publish. Triggered by "public surface audit", "did I leak anything", "check tracked files for private tokens", "private token scan", "public-surface-audit".

name: return-path-gate
description: Audits SKILL.md files in plugins/ for return-path gate compliance. Detects fire-and-forget chains where a caller dispatches a downstream skill but does not gate its next step on the callee's verdict. Reports each chain as CLOSED or OPEN and outputs specific fix suggestions. Triggered by "chain audit", "return-path check", "fire-and-forget detection", "chain closure audit", "skill chain compliance".

name: salience-splitter
description: Splits an over-loaded always-loaded context asset (SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md, memory index) into a lean resident layer plus an on-demand layer, by when content is needed rather than by length, linked by imperative pointers. Alias: skill-splitter. Triggers: "SKILL.md too large", "split this skill", "skill is bloated", "skill file too long", "CLAUDE.md 너무 커".

name: sim-conductor
description: Autonomously runs external user reaction simulations, internal audits, ideation scans, artifact validation, and quality reviews. Profiles the target artifact first, then derives task-appropriate personas, dispatches them as parallel agents, classifies findings into M/S/R tiers, and completes the pipeline through to commit automatically.

name: steel-quench
description: All-angle verification meta-skill for near-complete artifacts. Turns vague design anxiety into structured challenger waves using fh-commons:quench-challenger, then drives defense and convergence until root weaknesses, residual risks, and added complexity are explicit. Covers standard attack/defense rounds, optional Meta-Aware Adversary mode for AI-specific risks such as hallucination, context collapse, prompt injection, and tool lock-in, and Wave-P3 re-attack after an upstream gate declares PASS. Built-in outputs emphasize attack-plus-prescription pairs and can feed fh-meta:persona-innovator after convergence. Triggered by: "quench this", "devil's judgment", "all-angle review", "end-to-end verification", "steel quench", "deep pre-completion inspection", "did it really pass?".

name: verify-bidirectional
description: A skill that immediately updates the baseline and reflects it in the next session when the user raises a counter-argument to an AI recommendation. Triggered by "is that right?", "re-examine this", "something seems off here". Explicit /verify-bidirectional call also possible.

name: video-ingest
description: Ingests a video's content (YouTube and similar) for agent context, routing by capability, task need, and video length — a natively multimodal engine (Gemini via agy or the Gemini API) for direct-URL and long video, Claude vision over ffmpeg-extracted frames when no such engine is present, yt-dlp captions when the transcript alone suffices, and the logged-in claude-in-chrome session for auth-gated videos. The governor cross-checks any multimodal comprehensive-read. Triggered by "ingest this video", "what does this video show", "get the transcript from this YouTube video", "video-ingest".

name: preprep
description: 한국식 발표대본과 장표에 특화된 준비 하네스. 레퍼런스를 먼저 묻고(공식 장표가이드 · 참고 덱), 대화로 주제·구성·전개를 세운 뒤, 기승전결 배치안을 «여러 개» 내고 사람이 고른다. 제작 후 바닥 검사 — 금지 인용이 어느 면에 남았나, 원고와 노트의 단위 참조가 갈렸나, 재생성이 사람 편집을 삼켰나, 장 사이 의존이 깨졌나, 조어가 낭독면 첫 등장에 풀이를 달았나, 장당 발화가 상한을 넘었나. 리허설 녹화를 들으면 쉼·접속사·문장 끝 억양·끝인사 크기를 코칭 표로 낸다(advisory). Triggers "발표 준비", "발표 대본 만들어줘", "장표 점검해줘", "덱이랑 대본 어긋난 데 있나", "발표 자료 정합성", "리허설 대본 확인", "리허설 녹화 코칭해줘", "presentation prep".

name: qp
description: QP (Quality Platform) router — takes a web URL or a desktop app name and runs the plan → run → regress loop (qp-plan, qp-run, qp-regress) end to end, or routes to one stage. Classifies the target (public vs profile-required), probes which adapter the session has (Playwright MCP for web, computer-use MCP for desktop), and writes every artifact with a typed engine/adapter marker. Triggers on "test this website for me", "run a QA pass on this app", "check the app end to end", "이 사이트 QA 돌려줘", "이 앱 테스트해줘", "회귀 돌려줘".

name: qp-plan
description: Prepare stage of QP — builds a surface inventory of a web page or desktop app (routes, menus, forms, dialogs), checks it is MECE (no overlap, nothing missing that is visible), and designs test cases as a TSV with preconditions and expected values whose SOURCE is named. Works without a spec document (then expected values come from the inventory, not a plan). Triggers on "what should I test on this page", "make a test plan for this app", "list the screens of this app", "테스트 케이스 뽑아줘", "이 화면 인벤토리 만들어줘".

name: qp-regress
description: Regression stage of QP — re-executes a previous run's test cases unchanged, computes surface_reach (how many TCs left the entry screen, as a ratio over ALL TCs), and reports the per-TC delta against the earlier run so a "no change" claim is per case, not an aggregate. Triggers on "did anything regress since last run", "re-run last week's QA pass", "compare this run with the previous one", "회귀 확인해줘", "지난 런이랑 비교해줘".

name: qp-run
description: Automation stage of QP — executes the test cases from qp-plan against the live app through the session's adapter (Playwright MCP for web, computer-use MCP for desktop), records one verdict per step with a closed status, an MTM branch, whether the step was closed by machine evidence or left to judgment, and masks emails/tokens/passwords out of the evidence before saving. Triggers on "run these test cases", "execute the QA plan against the site", "drive the app through the TCs", "TC 실행해줘", "플랜대로 돌려줘".

name: todo-dev
description: todo/ 아래 파이썬 TODO CLI(add·list·done 명령, TODO_DB JSON 저장소)의 기능 추가, 버그 수정, 리팩터링, 테스트 작성, 검증을 조율하는 오케스트레이터. TODO CLI 관련 코드 작업 요청에 사용한다. 다시 실행, 재실행, 수정, 보완, 이전 결과 개선, QA만 다시 같은 후속 요청에도 사용한다. 단순 질문에는 사용하지 않는다.

name: meeting-notes-organize
description: 주간 회의록 원본(여러 파일 또는 한 파일)을 안건별 논의·결정 사항·액션 아이템·미결 사항으로 구조화해 정리하는 방법. 회의록 정리, 회의록 분류, 액션 아이템 추출, 정리본 수정·보완 요청 시 사용한다.

name: weekly-meeting-summary
description: 주간 회의록을 정리하고 요약 문서를 만드는 전체 작업을 조율하는 오케스트레이터. 회의록 요약, 주간 회의 정리, 주간 보고용 요약 요청 시 사용한다. 다시 실행, 재실행, 요약 수정·보완, 이전 결과를 바탕으로 한 개선, 정리만/검토만 다시 같은 후속 요청에도 사용한다.

name: weekly-summary-write
description: 정리된 회의록으로 주간 회의 요약 문서를 작성하는 형식과 문체 규칙. 주간 요약 작성, 요약 문서 수정·보완, 검토 의견 반영 시 사용한다.

name: todo-dev
description: TODO CLI 개발 작업(명령·기능 추가, 버그 수정, 테스트 작성, 리뷰, 커밋·push)을 개발자·테스터·리뷰어 에이전트 팀으로 진행하는 오케스트레이터. todo CLI, todo.json, todo/cli.py 관련 구현·수정·테스트 요청에 사용한다. 재실행, 수정, 보완, 이전 결과 개선, 테스트만 다시, 리뷰만 다시 요청에도 사용한다. 단순 질문에는 쓰지 않는다.

name: todo-dev-team
description: TODO CLI(todo/cli.py) 개발 작업을 개발자·테스터·리뷰어 팀으로 진행하는 오케스트레이터. 명령 추가, 버그 수정, 테스트 작성, 리팩터링, 커밋·푸시 요청에 사용한다. 다시 실행, 재실행, 수정, 보완, 리뷰 반영, 테스트만 다시 같은 후속 요청에도 사용한다. 단순 질문에는 쓰지 않는다.

name: todo-dev
description: TODO CLI(todo/cli.py)에 명령을 추가하거나 버그를 고치고 테스트를 작성하는 방법. todo 앱 코드 수정·기능 추가·테스트 작성·리팩터링 작업에 사용한다. 수정, 보완, 다시 구현 요청에도 사용한다.

name: todo-orchestrator
description: TODO CLI 프로젝트의 기능 추가·버그 수정·리팩터링·테스트 보강을 개발자와 QA 에이전트로 조율한다. todo 앱 관련 코드 작업 요청에 사용한다. 다시 실행, 재실행, 수정, 보완, 이전 결과 개선, QA만 다시 같은 후속 요청에도 사용한다. 단순 질문에는 사용하지 않는다.

name: aeo-page-audit
description: Audit any web page for Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) readiness - can AI crawlers reach it, and can AI engines extract answers from it. Use when asked "is this page AEO ready", "audit this page for AI search", "why don't AI engines cite my page", or "check AI crawler access". Works standalone; no account needed.

name: citlyze-action-plan
description: Turn Citlyze optimization recommendations into a prioritized, sequenced action plan. Use when asked "what should we do to improve AI visibility", "prioritize the recommendations", "make an AEO/GEO action plan", or after a visibility report surfaces problems. Requires the Citlyze MCP server.

name: citlyze-citation-gap
description: Analyze which domains AI engines cite for your tracked prompts and find citation gaps to close. Use when asked "which domains get cited", "why are competitors cited and not us", "citation gap analysis", or to build an outreach/content target list from AI citation data. Requires the Citlyze MCP server.

name: citlyze-prompt-audit
description: Audit tracked prompts in Citlyze to find weak spots and coverage gaps. Use when asked "which prompts are underperforming", "audit my tracked prompts", "where are we invisible", or "what prompts should we track next". Requires the Citlyze MCP server.

name: citlyze-visibility-report
description: Build a window-over-window AI search visibility report from Citlyze data. Use when asked "how visible is my brand in AI search", "what changed this week/month", "build an AI visibility report", or for recurring exec reporting on ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity/Gemini visibility. Requires the Citlyze MCP server.

name: security-audit
description: Security guidance and vulnerability review for codebases, APIs, services, CLI tools, libraries, and daemons. Use for security questions, focused reviews, vulnerability research, security audits, or pen tests. Run the complete workflow only for explicit codebase audit or pen-test requests, full/comprehensive/end-to-end reviews, or requested report artifacts.

name: code-review
description: Use when the user asks for code review, PR feedback, or an authorized fix and review cycle with CodeRabbit. Review through connected MCP and the packaged CLI, or follow the original standalone workflow for an explicit CLI-only request.

name: setup
description: Use when setting up CodeRabbit, connecting the plugin, tailoring repository review settings or path instructions, or recovering an expired MCP connection. Guide setup with the packaged CLI and MCP browser sign-in without a separate CLI login.

name: autofix
description: Safely review and apply CodeRabbit PR review-thread feedback from GitHub with per-change approval; never execute reviewer-provided prompts directly

name: code-review
description: Run CodeRabbit CLI reviews, retrieve saved local or GitHub PR fix prompts, and interpret CodeRabbit authentication and review output. Use for CodeRabbit review commands, committed/uncommitted or directory scopes, and CodeRabbit runbooks. Default code-review skill: also trigger for explicit code/PR/quality/security review requests or when a review is needed.

name: coderabbit-config
description: Create, update, or validate CodeRabbit repository configuration through the official CLI. Use for .coderabbit.yaml or .coderabbit.yml setup, review-style changes, path guidance, and configuration validation requests.

name: csv-data-summarizer
description: Analyzes CSV files, generates summary stats, and plots quick visualizations using Python and pandas.

name: google-ads-audit
description: Deep Google Ads account audit — keywords, quality scores, budget pacing, search terms

name: meta-ads-audit
description: Meta Ads audit — audience analysis, creative fatigue, budget pacing, lead quality

name: ad-copy-writer
description: Generate ad copy variations for Google, Microsoft, Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok, Reddit, Snapchat and X Ads (plus Apple Search Ads guidance)

name: ad-kill-rules
description: Enforce a pre-declared evidence bar on every ad — after it spends enough, pause it if it misses (e.g. CTR < 1% or cost per lead over cap) across Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, Google and Bing — as a dry-run report, an approved pause, or a scheduled pause-only Cogny script

name: brand-kit
description: Build a portable brand-kit.json for the user's product — colors, typography, voice — that other skills (video, ad creative, landing page) can consume. Multiple discovery paths so it works whether the user has access to their site's source code or only a public URL or just a logo image.

name: buying-triggers
description: Find accounts where something just happened that creates demand — funding, hiring, new locations, launches, rising ad engagement — skip anyone already in your pipeline, and draft outreach only when "this event creates this problem, and we solve it this way" comes out sharp

name: campaign-ledger
description: Give every campaign an ID and carry it everywhere — allocate IDs, audit ad/email/UTM naming across Google, Meta, LinkedIn, Bing, TikTok and X, and keep one ledger joining spend → leads → deals → revenue per campaign ID

name: closed-lost-revival
description: Re-read every lost deal in your CRM (HubSpot, Pipedrive or Upsales; Salesforce via the CRM layer) with its calls, meetings and notes, replace "not interested" with the real reason plus a reopen condition, then watch for those conditions — a shipped feature, a renewal date, a champion moving, the account coming back to your site — and draft a personal note that quotes the original conversation

name: cogny
description: Run Cogny marketing analysis tasks — fetch scheduled tasks, analyze ad accounts via MCP, report findings

name: community-pulse
description: Weekly read on community health — Discord joins, active channels, top contributors, themes and unanswered questions, plus Crisp support conversations and YouTube comments when connected

name: competitor-analysis
description: Research competitor positioning, ads, pricing, and market gaps

name: avoid-ai-writing
description: Audit and rewrite content to remove AI writing patterns ("AI-isms"). Use this skill when asked to "remove AI-isms," "clean up AI writing," "edit writing for AI patterns," "audit writing for AI tells," or "make this sound less like AI." Supports a detect-only mode, an edit-in-place mode for files, an optional voice profile (casual / professional / technical / warm / blunt), and an iterate-to-convergence pass.

name: ai-writing-detector
description: Use when the user asks to detect, scan, audit, score, or flag AI-writing patterns without rewriting the text, including requests for a deterministic local detector result when the host can execute Node.

name: avoid-ai-writing-router
description: Use when a request combines AI-writing audit, rewrite, file editing, voice preservation, false-positive interpretation, verification, or when the user invokes Avoid AI Writing without naming a mode.

name: false-positive-reviewer
description: Use when a user asks what AI-writing flags mean, whether detector output proves AI authorship, or wants a careful interpretation of possible false positives, especially for academic, hiring, publication, disciplinary, or other consequential decisions.

name: file-edit-in-place
description: Use when the user names a local file and explicitly asks to clean, rewrite, humanize, or remove AI-writing patterns in that file itself, with minimal targeted edits and post-edit verification.

name: preservation-verifier
description: Use when the user provides an original and rewritten version, asks whether a rewrite preserved protected content, or wants a deterministic check for code, frontmatter, quotes, tables, links, paths, numbers, headings, and residual AI-pattern regressions.

name: voice-preserving-rewriter
description: Use when the user asks to rewrite, humanize, clean up, or remove AI-isms from text while preserving the writer's voice, facts, intent, structure, register, and protected material.

name: ios-simulator-skill
description: Build, test, and drive iOS apps in the Simulator with 31 token-efficient scripts. Use when asked to build or test an Xcode project, launch an app on a simulator, tap/type/swipe through its UI by accessibility label, take screenshots or visual diffs, audit accessibility, read logs or diagnose hangs, or manage simulators (boot, erase, permissions, location, push, appearance). macOS only; needs Xcode, Python 3.12+ and idb.

name: ab-testing
description: When the user wants to plan, run, or read A/B tests, or asks a judgement call on one: is the result real, can we stop, which version won, is this worth testing at all: sample size, duration, significance, hypotheses, and experiment backlogs. For tracking setup, see analytics. For page-level conversion fixes, see cro.

name: ad-creative
description: When the user wants to write or judge ad creative, or asks which ad, hook, or angle to run or kill: headlines, primary text, and variations for Google, Meta, LinkedIn, and TikTok, fresh angles when creative fatigues. Test hypotheses name the metric, comparison, and expected direction. No AI tells like 'it's not X, it's Y'. For campaign strategy, see ads. For landing pages, see copywriting.

name: ads
description: When the user wants to plan, run, or fix paid ads on Google, Meta, and LinkedIn, or asks a judgement call on them: are ads worth it, which channel or budget split, why CPA rose, kill or keep a campaign. End with facts, hypotheses, and missing data; label unavailable inputs MISSING instead of estimating. For ad copy, see ad-creative. For pixels and CAPI, see conversion-tracking. For landing pages, see cro.

name: ai-seo
description: When the user wants to get cited and recommended in AI answers (ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overviews), or asks why AI cites a competitor, which content gets cited, or whether llms.txt or a page format is worth it: AEO, GEO, AI visibility, agent-readable sites. For technical and on-page SEO, see seo-audit. For structured data, see schema.

name: analytics
description: When the user wants to set up or audit analytics, or asks whether a metric or number is calculated right, what to track, or how to name events: tracking plans, GA4, GTM, Mixpanel, PostHog, UTMs. Rate metrics divide matching closed windows, never full-period spend by partial-period results. For conversions in ad platforms, see conversion-tracking. For attribution or platforms that over-claim, see attribution. For tests, see ab-testing.

name: aso
description: When the user wants to audit or optimize an App Store or Google Play listing, or asks which title, keywords, or screenshots to pick or why downloads are low: subtitle, description, ratings, and comparing listings with competitors.

name: attribution
description: When the user wants to work out which marketing drives revenue, or asks whether a channel is really working, which numbers to trust, or how to credit podcasts and dark social: attribution models, platforms that over-claim, MMM, incrementality and holdout tests, self-reported attribution. For tracking and UTMs, see analytics. For pixels and CAPI, see conversion-tracking. For CRM revenue, see revops. For AI search blind spots, see ai-seo.

name: churn-prevention
description: When the user wants to reduce churn, or asks why customers cancel, whether to offer a discount or pause: cancellation flows, exit surveys, save offers, dunning and failed-payment recovery. For win-back emails, see emails. For in-app upgrade screens, see paywalls.

name: co-marketing
description: When the user wants co-marketing partners or joint campaigns, or asks whether a partner fits, a size mismatch matters, or how to split work and leads: integration partners, cross-promotion, co-branded content, joint webinars. For referral programs, see referrals. For launch partnerships, see launch. For running the event, see events.

name: cold-email
description: When the user wants to write or run B2B cold outbound, or asks whether an opener, reason to reach out, or email works or why nobody replies: cold emails, follow-ups, sending domains, deliverability, LinkedIn, cadences. Send from secondary domains, verify lists first, turn off open tracking, stop every channel when a prospect replies. No AI tells like 'it's not X, it's Y'. For the list, see prospecting. For lifecycle email, see emails. For call scripts, see sales-enablement.

name: community-marketing
description: When the user wants to build or grow an online community, or asks whether a community is worth it, where to host it, or why members stay quiet: Discord, Slack, forums, participation, community-led growth, advocates. For referral programs, see referrals. For creator partnerships, see influencer-marketing.

name: competitor-profiling
description: When the user wants to research competitors into dated profiles, or asks what a rival charges, claims, or is doing, or whether a conclusion about them is fair: positioning, pricing, features, reviews, SEO, observed facts kept apart from inference. For comparison pages, see competitors. For battle cards, see sales-enablement. For accounts you sell to, see prospecting. For how a competitor grew, see reverse-engineer-marketing.

name: competitors
description: When the user wants to create or audit comparison and alternative pages ('X vs Y', 'X alternative', 'best X alternatives'), or asks what a public page may say about a competitor: page formats, fair claims, and outdated pages. For researching competitors, see competitor-profiling. For internal battle cards, see sales-enablement.

name: content-strategy
description: When the user wants to plan content, or asks which topic or piece to prioritize, what to write about, or why posts bring no customers: topic clusters, editorial calendars, roadmaps tied to customers and search. For writing pieces, see copywriting. For SEO audits, see seo-audit. For social content, see social.

name: conversion-tracking
description: When the user wants to set up, audit, or fix conversion tracking to Google Ads, Meta, GA4, LinkedIn, and TikTok, or asks why conversions are missing or doubled: GTM, pixels, CAPI, Enhanced Conversions, offline imports. Fire on confirmed success, not the submit click; verify a test conversion arrives; diagnose before changing; offer free paths and disclose partner tools. For tracking plans, see analytics. For attribution, see attribution. For bidding, see ads.

name: copy-editing
description: When the user wants to edit, tighten, proofread, or refresh existing copy, or asks whether to keep, cut, or change a line in it, without rewriting from scratch. Every edit removes AI tells: 'it's not X, it's Y' reveals, 'no X, no Y, no Z' lists, and sentences that trail into extra comma clauses. A request to fix one line gets a point edit to that line only. For new copy, see copywriting.

name: copywriting
description: When the user wants to write or rewrite page copy (homepage, landing, pricing, feature), or asks which headline, promise, or message to lead with. Diagnoses the input first (blank brief, real voice, or point edit) and changes only what it calls for. Claims must be supportable; a declined claim names the evidence that would unlock it. No AI tells like 'it's not X, it's Y' or 'no X, no Y, no Z'. For editing, see copy-editing. For emails, see emails. For the offer, see offers.

name: cro
description: When the user wants more conversions from a page or form, or asks why a page isn't converting, what to change first, or whether to add or remove a field or element: landing and pricing pages, lead forms, or a URL shared for feedback. For signup flows, see signup. For activation, see onboarding. For popups, see popups. For running the test, see ab-testing.

name: customer-research
description: When the user wants to run or synthesize customer research, or asks what customer quotes, reviews, or feedback really mean, what is safe to conclude, and what to ask next: interviews, surveys, voice of customer, personas, JTBD, mining Reddit and reviews. For copy from research, see copywriting. For acting on it in pages, see cro.

name: directory-submissions

For the broader launch, see launch. For other link building, see link-building.

name: emails

No AI tells like 'it's not X, it's Y', 'no X, no Y, no Z' lists, or fake 'Re:' subject lines. For cold outreach, see cold-email. For in-app onboarding, see onboarding. For texts, see sms.

name: events

For launches, see launch. For joint webinars, see co-marketing. For community programs, see community-marketing. For podcasts, see public-relations. For event emails, see emails.

name: image
description: When the user wants to create, generate, edit, or optimize marketing images, or asks which approach to take (generate, design, or photograph): blog heroes, social graphics, product mockups, banners, OG images. For ad images, see ad-creative. For video, see video.

name: influencer-marketing
description: When the user wants creator, influencer, or ambassador partnerships, or asks which creators fit, what to pay, which rights to buy, or whether a sponsorship worked: vetting, contracts, briefs, UGC, newsletter and podcast sponsorships, FTC disclosure. For affiliate payouts, see referrals. For community advocacy, see community-marketing. For creator content as ads, see ad-creative.

name: launch
description: When the user wants to plan a product or feature launch, or asks whether it's ready, when to announce, or how to get noticed: Product Hunt, beta and early access, waitlists, release go-to-market, launch checklists, release notes. For marketing after launch, see marketing-ideas. For the offer, see offers.

name: lead-magnets
description: When the user wants to plan or improve a lead magnet, or asks what to give away for emails or how much to ask in return (gating, form fields): checklists, templates, ebooks, gated guides, content upgrades. For interactive tools, see free-tools. For the follow-up sequence, see emails. For popups that capture emails, see popups.

name: link-building
description: When the user wants backlinks and mentions that lift rankings and AI citations, or asks how to get sites to link or whether a link tactic is safe: link gaps, unlinked mentions, broken links, guest posts, best-of outreach. Never buy links that pass ranking credit: paid or exchanged placements get rel=sponsored or nofollow. For press, see public-relations. For directories, see directory-submissions. For reviews, see referrals. For communities, see community-marketing.

name: marketing-council

To execute, hand off to the relevant skill.

name: marketing-ideas
description: When the user wants marketing ideas or growth tactics for a software product, or asks what to try to get attention or the next customers with little time or budget, or after the obvious channels. Draws on a library of 139 ideas. For a specific channel, see that skill (ads, social, emails, and others). For a full plan, see marketing-plan.

name: marketing-loops
description: When the user wants a recurring marketing job an AI agent runs on a cadence or trigger, or asks what a weekly or daily automated check should do, remember, and when it should stop: SEO and ads checks, churn watches, outbound triage. For one-off ideas, see marketing-ideas. For the test loop, see ab-testing.

name: marketing-plan
description: When the user wants a full marketing or go-to-market plan for a client, an advised company, or their own product, or asks how to sequence or prioritize several initiatives with a fixed team and budget: channels, budget, team, goals across AARRR, market sizing. For positioning first, see product-marketing. For ideas only, see marketing-ideas.

name: marketing-psychology
description: When the user wants to apply psychology to marketing, or asks why buyers behave or value things as they do, or whether a persuasion tactic is honest: biases, mental models, anchoring, social proof, scarcity, loss aversion, framing. For a page, see cro. For pricing tactics, see pricing. For copy, see copywriting.

name: offers
description: When the user wants to design or improve the offer itself, or asks why it isn't selling or how to add urgency honestly: value stacking, bonuses, guarantees, scarcity, payment plans, upsells. Best for services, courses, coaching, and high-ticket B2B; for self-serve SaaS, read pricing first. For price and tiers, see pricing. For the page, see copywriting. For the launch, see launch. For sales collateral, see sales-enablement.

name: onboarding
description: When the user wants better onboarding and activation, or asks why new users don't stick or what the first session should do: first-run experience, aha moments, checklists, empty states, time to value. For the signup flow itself, see signup. For onboarding emails, see emails.

name: paywalls
description: When the user wants to create or improve in-app paywalls and upgrade moments, or asks when or how hard to ask free users to pay (after they've seen value): upgrade screens, upsell modals, feature gates, limit-reached and trial-expired screens, mobile subscription paywalls. For public pricing pages, see cro. For pricing decisions, see pricing.

name: popups
description: When the user wants to create or improve popups, modals, slide-ins, sticky bars, and banners, or asks whether one will help or annoy and when to show it: exit intent, email capture, scroll and time triggers, announcements. For forms and pages outside popups, see cro.

name: pricing
description: When the user wants to set pricing and packaging, or asks what to charge, whether to raise prices, or how to move existing customers: tiers, value metrics, per-seat vs usage, freemium and trials, willingness to pay, pricing pages. For in-app upgrade screens, see paywalls. For offers on services, courses, and high-ticket B2B, see offers.

name: product-marketing
description: When the user wants to create or update the product marketing context doc (.agents/product-marketing.md), or asks what belongs in it or whether positioning or ICP is clear enough: product, ICP, positioning, competitors, customer language, brand voice. Use it before other marketing skills on a new project, when the audience or positioning changes, and to log learnings.

name: programmatic-seo
description: When the user wants SEO pages at scale from templates and data, or asks whether a page set will rank or look thin: location, integration, comparison, directory, and '[X] for [Y]' pages, each useful rather than thin. For SEO audits, see seo-audit. For content planning, see content-strategy.

name: prospecting
description: When the user wants to find and qualify prospects for outbound, or asks who to target first, which signal to prioritize, or where to spot buyers with the problem: buying signals, enrichment, verification, account research. Verify emails before a sequence, never scrape LinkedIn: define audiences in Sales Navigator and pull contacts from licensed data. For outreach, see cold-email. For competitor research, see competitor-profiling.

name: public-relations
description: When the user wants press and media coverage, or asks what to say to a reporter, whether a story is newsworthy, or how to handle a crisis: pitches, press releases, media lists, HARO, op-eds, podcast guest prep, newsjacking (public relations, not pull requests). For directories, see directory-submissions. For launches, see launch. For cold outreach to prospects, see cold-email.

name: referrals
description: When the user wants referral and affiliate programs or word of mouth, or asks what to reward, how much to pay, or which loop to start with: refer-a-friend incentives, commissions and payouts, partner programs, 'made with' badges, review campaigns. For launch virality, see launch. For creator deals, see influencer-marketing.

name: reverse-engineer-marketing
description: When the user wants to know how another company grew and what to copy, or asks what a competitor did and when: a dated log of their moves against their traffic from public data, archives, job posts, reviews, and their funnel, compared with the user's data, ending in plays routed to other skills. Also finds where competitors are weak. For a snapshot profile, see competitor-profiling. For comparison pages, see competitors.

name: revops
description: When the user wants to design revenue operations, or asks when a lead is ready for sales or why sales and marketing disagree on lead quality: lifecycle stages, MQL and SQL, scoring, routing, handoff, pipeline stages, CRM automation. For outbound copy, see cold-email. For email flows, see emails.

name: sales-enablement
description: When the user wants sales collateral, or asks what to give a champion or rep, or how to answer an objection or make the case: decks, one-pagers, objection handling, demo scripts, talk tracks, battle cards, proposals, win-loss. For public comparison pages, see competitors. For buyer research, see customer-research. For website copy, see copywriting. For cold emails, see cold-email. For the offer, see offers.

name: schema
description: When the user wants to add, fix, or validate schema markup (JSON-LD), or asks which type fits a page or whether some markup is allowed: product, review, recipe, FAQ, rich result eligibility (FAQ no longer earns Google rich results), Search Console errors. For broader SEO, see seo-audit. For AI search, see ai-seo.

name: seo-audit
description: When the user wants to audit or diagnose SEO, or asks why traffic dropped, a page won't rank, or whether a setup like canonicals, hreflang, or redirects is right: technical SEO, indexing, Google updates, on-page and titles, Core Web Vitals, local SEO. Start here when someone just says their SEO is bad. For pages at scale, see programmatic-seo. For structured data, see schema. For AI search, see ai-seo.

name: signup

It can transcribe or subtitle files and YouTube, X, TikTok or Twitch links; generate images from a text prompt, edit or upscale them, remove backgrounds and read text from images (OCR); turn text or a photo into video and describe videos; read text aloud, also in the user's own voice cloned from a short sample; make music; compute embeddings; and improve prompts for image and video generators. Use when the user wants any of this done now, unless they name another provider. Quotes the price before every paid job. Also connects the deAPI MCP server to an agent and reports the key's limits, balance and spending. Not for chat, summaries or other LLM text generation.

name: deapi-api
description: Builds apps on deAPI: native API, OpenAI SDKs, webhooks. Helps developers add deAPI image, video, speech, music, transcription, OCR and embedding features to their own code, through the native API v2 (jobs and polling, price quotes, webhooks, WebSockets, rate limits, errors, keys and usage) or OpenAI SDKs pointed at https://oai.deapi.ai/v1 (also from LangChain, LlamaIndex, LiteLLM or the Vercel AI SDK). Use when writing, reviewing or debugging application code that calls deAPI, choosing between the native API and the OpenAI-compatible API, verifying webhook signatures, or reading cost and usage per key.

name: algorithmic-color-palette
description: Derive a full UI palette from one or two brand colours — state variants, brand-tinted greys, semantic colours. Use when building or expanding a colour system.

name: app-shell
description: Top bar, sidebar rail, app launcher, tenant and environment cue, status bar. Use when designing the persistent shell, a collapsible sidebar, or navigation between apps behind one login.

name: authentic-product-representation
description: Product visuals must show the real product with real data. Use when building landing pages, hero sections, screenshots or demo panels.

name: brand-visual-language
description: Shape language across type, radius and icons carries brand personality. Use when starting a design system, picking icons or radius tokens, or reviewing visual consistency.

name: button-states
description: Rest, hover, active, focus, disabled and loading states, derived from the base colour. Use when designing buttons, links, inputs or any clickable component.

name: clone-website
description: Rebuild a live web page 1:1 from measurement into Figma, Penpot or code, then verify it. Use when reproducing a page or checking a rebuild against the original.

name: color-mode-and-theme
description: Light, dark or both, and when a theme selector is worth it. Use when defining a base palette or deciding on dark mode support.

name: component-family-consistency
description: Buttons, inputs, badges and pills share radius, colour logic, shadow, border and spacing. Use when building, changing or reviewing UI components or a component library.

name: coordinated-data-views
description: Show a table and its map, diagram, timeline or chart together, with selection synced both ways. Use when data appears in two representations at once.

name: data-display-and-selection
description: View modes, row selection, mass actions, sorting, filters, search and table patterns. Use when designing data tables, listings, file browsers or any collection.

name: dembrandt
description: Orchestrator that routes a UI/UX task through brand, tokens, layout, components, polish and accessibility. Use for multi-concern work such as a design review, UI build or interface audit.

name: domain-expert-configuration
description: Settings for experts who are not developers — domain language, sane defaults, grouping by professional concept. Use when designing settings panels, solver configuration or constraint editors.

name: elevation-and-depth
description: Shadows and layering that lift elements above the surface. Use when designing cards, dropdowns, modals, tooltips or any floating element.

name: extract-design
description: Extract colours, typography, spacing, components and W3C design tokens from a live website with Dembrandt. Use when you need a site's real tokens or want to seed a design system from it.

name: form-design
description: Helper text, placeholders, validation and submit behaviour. Use when designing or reviewing a form, input field or data entry UI.

name: generate-ui-from-brand
description: Pipeline from a URL or DESIGN.md to tokens, decisions and a UI spec. Use when building UI for an existing brand, auditing a design system or fixing visual inconsistency.

name: gestalt-ui-organisation
description: Group controls with Gestalt principles so users see what belongs together. Use when laying out components, navigation, toolbars, forms or dashboards.

name: global-toolbar-controls
description: Currency, language, region and unit selectors live in a low-profile header or footer spot. Use when designing locale switchers or product-wide preference controls.

name: information-architecture
description: Naming, navigation, a UI that mirrors the data model, confirms for irreversible changes. Use when structuring a large application or naming its entities.

name: layout-paradigms-and-consistency
description: Choose a layout paradigm (feed, board, table, canvas, master-detail, dashboard) and reuse it across screens. Includes a landing page narrative framework. Use when structuring a screen, page template or landing page.

name: loading-states-and-perceived-performance
description: Spinners, skeletons and staggered reveals that manage wait times. Use when designing loading states, async data or the feel of a slow interface.

name: marketing-vs-product-system
description: A marketing site and its product may differ in density and scale but share one token layer. Use when the two drift apart, share components or need a single token owner.

name: micro-interactions
description: Small purposeful animations — toggles, animated icons, success moments. Use when designing interactive feedback, success states or loaders.

name: modal-and-overlay-patterns
description: Modals, drawers, bottom sheets and popovers, each with its scope and blocking level. Use when designing dialogs, confirmations, side panels or action sheets.

name: modular-scale-typography
description: Ratio-based type scale where every size relates to the others. Use when defining font sizes or type tokens, or when typography feels arbitrary.

name: motion-and-storytelling
description: Disney's animation principles and cinematic technique applied to UI motion. Use when designing transitions, scroll animations or onboarding motion.

name: nielsen-usability-heuristics
description: Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics. Use when auditing an interface, designing interaction flows, writing error messages or reviewing usability.

name: notifications-and-recovery
description: Toasts, inline errors, banners and recovery paths. Use when designing error states, success confirmations, async feedback or in-place editing.

name: operational-expert-tool-ui
description: Dense, linear, status-at-a-glance UI for specialists who use a tool all day. Use when designing dispatch, warehouse, logistics, scheduling or other B2B operations tools.

name: performance-and-web-vitals
description: Lighthouse audits and Core Web Vitals — LCP, CLS, INP. Use when optimising page load, layout shift, input delay, images, fonts or render-blocking resources.

name: real-world-metaphors
description: Cards, drawers, carousels and other patterns borrowed from the physical world. Use when designing layout patterns, gestures or navigation paradigms.

name: repeated-component-alignment
description: Cards, rows, tiles and cells are fixed slot models that stay aligned when content length varies. Use when building or reviewing any repeated component.

name: responsive-paradigms
description: Mobile, tablet and desktop are different paradigms, not one layout scaled. Use when designing responsive layouts or deciding what each breakpoint shows.

name: scroll-areas
description: Avoid inner scroll containers; when unavoidable, one axis at a time. Use when a layout, table or panel might scroll inside the page.

name: semantic-html-and-seo
description: Semantic HTML5, SEO basics, alt text, progressive enhancement and SPA concerns. Use when building web UI, reviewing markup or optimising for search.

name: sizing-units
description: rem, px or relative units for each kind of value. Use when defining spacing and sizing tokens, control heights or media queries, or when a layout breaks under enlarged text.

name: status-colors-and-errors
description: Few semantic colours, each meaning one thing, and errors with a way forward. Use when designing status indicators, validation, alerts or error states.

name: sticky-and-fixed-elements
description: Sticky headers, bottom toolbars, floating action buttons and pinned table headers. Use when deciding what stays on screen while the user scrolls.

name: surface-separation
description: Set a surface apart by one means — border, elevation or fill — and keep opacity for state. Use when designing cards, panels, list rows, toolbars or any container.

name: tab-navigation
description: Tabs swap views under a shared context. Use when designing tabbed layouts, settings pages, detail views or dashboards with several data views.

name: ui-context-and-scope
description: Show where the user is and what their actions affect — breadcrumbs, regions, scope labels. Use when designing deep navigation or multi-section layouts.

name: ui-density
description: Match information density to platform and user type. Use when designing data tables, dashboards or toolbars, or adapting a desktop product for mobile.

name: user-flows-and-guided-paths
description: Guided multi-step paths and wizards. Use when designing onboarding, checkout, setup sequences or any multi-step journey.

name: visual-emphasis-and-hierarchy
description: Size, colour, weight and position mark what matters most. Use when designing button groups, CTAs, cards, dashboards or any layout with a primary action.

name: wcag-accessibility
description: WCAG 2.2 AA compliance as required by the European Accessibility Act. Use when designing, building or reviewing any user-facing interface for accessibility.

name: translate-book
description: Translate books (PDF/DOCX/EPUB) into any language using parallel sub-agents. Converts input -> Markdown chunks -> translated chunks -> HTML/DOCX/EPUB/PDF.

name: acestep
description: AI music generation with ACE-Step 1.5 — background music, vocal tracks, covers, stem extraction, audio repainting, and continuation for video production. Use when generating music, soundtracks, jingles, or working with audio stems. Triggers include background music, soundtrack, jingle, music generation, stem extraction, cover, style transfer, repaint, continuation, or musical composition tasks.

name: blender
description: 3D scenes, character acting and product shots from a shot spec, rendered in Blender, as a finished film, as clips for any other build (moviepy, a video job, an editor), or as elements of a Remotion video (transparent characters over a scene, a Remotion render on a 3D laptop, phone or floating card that the camera pulls back from, an imported 3D model on a studio stage), or a brand's opening and closing ident built from its SVG logo. A rigged cartoon cast described in JSON (build, face, hair, clothes, a seed), sets, shots by type, acting beats in seconds or on narration words, every camera checked by geometry, sound placed on the motion. Use when a video needs a consistent directable character (parody, explainer gag, reaction shot), a 3D reveal or element in a Remotion video, a device or product shot of an app or a model, or exact acting timing that AI video clips can't hold. Triggers include Blender, 3D, character animation, rigged character, cast, shot spec, acting, camera angles, transparent clip, alpha, pull out from the screen, phone mockup, device mockup, product shot, turntable, orbit, glTF, GLB, BlenderClip, logo animation, ident, logo reveal, sting, SVG in 3D.

name: elevenlabs
description: Generate AI voiceovers, sound effects, and music using ElevenLabs APIs. Use when creating audio content for videos, podcasts, or games. Triggers include generating voiceovers, narration, dialogue, sound effects from descriptions, background music, soundtrack generation, voice cloning, or any audio synthesis task.

name: ffmpeg
description: Video and audio processing with FFmpeg. Use for format conversion, resizing, compression, audio extraction, and preparing assets for Remotion. Triggers include converting GIF to MP4, resizing video, extracting audio, compressing files, or any media transformation task.

name: ideogram4
description: Prompting patterns for Ideogram 4 text-to-image — best-in-class in-image text rendering and exact color/layout control via structured JSON captions. Use when generating images that need legible on-image text (title cards, thumbnails, logos, signage, CTAs), precise brand colors, or controlled spatial layout. Triggers include title slide image, thumbnail with text, on-image text, legible text in image, brand color palette image, bounding-box layout, Ideogram.

name: ltx2
description: AI video generation with LTX-2.3 22B — text-to-video, image-to-video clips for video production. Use when generating video clips, animating images, creating b-roll, animated backgrounds, or motion content. Triggers include video generation, animate image, b-roll, motion, video clip, text-to-video, image-to-video.

name: moviepy
description: Python video composition with moviepy 2.x — overlaying deterministic text on AI-generated video (LTX-2, SadTalker), compositing clips, single-file build.py video projects. Use when adding labels/captions/lower-thirds to LTX-2 or SadTalker outputs, building short ad-style spots in pure Python without Remotion, or doing programmatic video composition. Triggers include text overlay on video, label LTX-2 clip, caption SadTalker output, lower third, build.py video, moviepy, Python video composition, sub-30s ad spot.

name: parody-short
description: Comedy shorts about a group's own life - a team's launch, quarter end, office move or leaving do; a club's season; a class's year; a family's Christmas - or about a shared topic everyone recognises (video calls, the return to the office), told in a borrowed genre (80s action intro, creature feature, Dickens Christmas ad, heist, nature documentary) and starring the group's real, animated photos or an invented cast. Covers mining the group's own context for in-jokes (chat, email, calendars, shared docs, plus domain tools like a CRM, helpdesk or git), mapping a genre's beats onto the real event, costuming and animating photos (image_edit then LTX), and per-genre look and sound. Use when someone asks for a fun, parody, spoof, holiday or "for the giggles" video about their team, colleagues, club, class or family, a party or all-hands video, or wants people's photos animated into a story.

name: playwright-recording
description: Record browser interactions as video using Playwright. Use for capturing demo videos, app walkthroughs, and UI flows for Remotion videos. Triggers include recording a demo, capturing browser video, screen recording a website, or creating walkthrough footage.

name: qwen-edit
description: AI image editing prompting patterns for Qwen-Image (Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 by default, Qwen-Image-2.1 as a non-commercial Modal opt-in). Use when editing photos while preserving identity, reframing cropped images, changing clothing or accessories, adjusting poses, applying style transfers, or character transformations. Provides prompt patterns, parameter tuning, and examples.

name: remotion
description: Toolkit-specific Remotion patterns — custom transitions, shared components, and project conventions. For core Remotion framework knowledge (hooks, animations, rendering, etc.), see the `remotion-official` skill.

name: runpod
description: Cloud GPU processing via RunPod serverless. Use when setting up RunPod endpoints, deploying Docker images, managing GPU resources, troubleshooting endpoint issues, or understanding costs. Covers all 5 toolkit images (qwen-edit, realesrgan, propainter, sadtalker, qwen3-tts).

name: synthetic-ui-demo
description: Product demo and release-notes videos with no screen recording. Rebuild the app's screens as static React from its source code, then drive them in Remotion with a scripted cursor and camera (lib/components Stage + Cursor). Use when making a product walkthrough, feature demo, release-notes or changelog video for an app whose source you can read, or when a Playwright recording would be flaky, need test data, or go stale. Triggers include synthetic demo, rebuild the UI, release video, feature walkthrough, product demo from source, scripted cursor, camera zoom on UI, no screen recording.

name: video-design
description: Visual design for videos - colour by act, type scale, chart and layout rules for 16:9 and 9:16 scenes, a design.md handoff that any design skill can fill, and a contact-sheet critique of the render. Use when designing or refining how a video looks (title cards, data scenes, slides, a whole video's palette), when a scene looks generic or busy, when choosing colours for a video, or when /design or /scene-review asks for visual work. Works on its own with a brand, or takes direction from a design source such as taste-skill, Anthropic's frontend-design, or the user's own design skill.

name: youtube-stats
description: How published videos are doing on YouTube, and what to learn from it. Views, likes, comments and subscribers per video, plus watch time, retention and traffic sources (Shorts feed, search, external) with the Analytics scope, saved as snapshots so trends show; GitHub traffic beside it to see whether YouTube sends people to the repo. Use when asked how a video or the channel is doing, which title, cover or genre worked, whether to make more of something, or for a weekly stats check.

name: video_toolkit
description: Make short explainer videos from a brief with claude-code-video-toolkit — submit a scene spec, poll a job, get a QC-checked MP4. Also covers the individual tools (AI voiceover, images, clips, music, talking heads) for custom work.

name: learn-from-materials
description: Turn books, PDFs, slides, documents, web pages and text into a source-grounded knowledge base, interactive learning HTML and Markdown in English or Chinese. Use for learning, summaries, explanations, review, quizzes, relationship maps, saving reusable methodology files, retrieving or comparing accumulated methods, and applying them to a real problem. 将材料转为可追溯知识库与交互学习页，支持中英文、关系图、方法论保存/检索/比较及应用；区分材料依据、推断与外部核验。

name: alipay-upload
description: 使用 social-auto-upload 的 `sau alipay` 登录支付宝生活号并发布视频。Use when 用户要向支付宝生活号发布视频或检查创作账号状态。

name: baijiahao-upload
description: 使用 social-auto-upload 的 `sau baijiahao` 登录百家号、检查账号并发布视频。Use when 用户要向百家号发布视频或核验百家号登录状态。

name: bilibili-upload
description: 当 agent 需要通过已安装的 `sau` CLI 完成 Bilibili 登录、账号校验或视频上传时使用这个 skill。优先使用 `sau bilibili ...`，程序会自动准备 `biliup`，不要求用户手动安装。

name: dayu-upload
description: 通过 social-auto-upload 的 sau CLI 完成大鱼号登录、账号核验、视频和文章的立即或定时发布，以及原作品结果查询。文章接收 HTML、Markdown 或 TXT 文件，Markdown 可选择主题。适用于已安装 sau 的环境，无需先阅读上传器源码。

name: douyin-upload
description: 当 agent 需要通过已安装的 `sau` CLI 完成抖音登录、cookie 校验、视频上传或图文发布时使用这个 skill。该 skill 适用于已经安装 `social-auto-upload` 且可调用 `sau` 命令的环境。优先使用这个 skill 进行稳定的命令式抖音工作流，而不是一开始就阅读 uploader 源码。

name: facebook-upload
description: 使用 sau CLI 登录 Facebook 个人主页，立即发布视频或图文，查询原作品、移至垃圾箱或永久删除。

name: hupu-upload
description: 使用 social-auto-upload 的 `sau hupu` 登录虎扑并发布视频，可指定封面。Use when 用户要向虎扑发布视频或检查虎扑账号状态。

name: instagram-upload
description: 使用 sau CLI 在 Instagram 独立网页登录、立即发布 Reels/单图/轮播、核验原作品并移至最近删除。

name: kuaishou-upload
description: 当 agent 需要通过已安装的 `sau` CLI 完成快手登录、cookie 校验、视频上传或图文发布时使用这个 skill。该 skill 适用于已经安装 `social-auto-upload` 且可调用 `sau` 命令的环境。优先使用这个 skill 进行稳定的命令式快手工作流，而不是一开始就阅读 uploader 源码。

name: meta-upload
description: 使用 sau CLI 登录 Facebook Page，发布视频或图文、设置北京时间排期、查询原作品并删除。

name: social-auto-upload
description: 为 social-auto-upload 提供总入口，按平台和内容类型选择对应发布流程。Use when 用户要在本仓库支持的平台发布视频、文章或图文，或需要把内容分发到多个指定平台。

name: tencent-upload
description: 使用 social-auto-upload 的 `sau tencent` 登录视频号并发布或定时发布视频、保存草稿。Use when 用户要向微信视频号发布视频或检查视频号账号状态。

name: tiktok-upload
description: 使用仓库现有 Patchright/Playwright Chrome 上传器登录并发布 TikTok 视频。Use when 用户要发布 TikTok 视频，且当前环境可访问本仓库及其本地 Chrome 配置。

name: weibo-upload
description: 使用 social-auto-upload 的 `sau weibo` 登录微博并发布视频，可指定封面。Use when 用户要向微博发布视频或检查微博账号状态。

name: xiaohongshu-upload
description: 当 agent 需要通过已安装的 `sau` CLI 完成小红书登录、cookie 校验、视频上传或图文发布时使用这个 skill。该 skill 适用于已经安装 `social-auto-upload` 且可调用 `sau` 命令的环境。优先使用这个 skill 进行稳定的命令式小红书工作流，而不是一开始就阅读 uploader 源码。

name: xueqiu-upload
description: 通过 social-auto-upload 的 sau CLI 登录和核验雪球账号，发布 HTML、Markdown 或 TXT 长文，保留原稿段间配图、原生文字结构与独立封面，并查询原作品确认结果。适用于雪球创作者平台，不支持定时或视频。

name: youtube-upload
description: 使用 social-auto-upload 的 `sau youtube` 登录 YouTube 并上传、安排定时或设置视频可见范围。Use when 用户要向 YouTube 发布或定时发布视频，或检查 Google/YouTube 登录状态。

name: zhihu-upload
description: 使用 social-auto-upload 的 sau CLI 登录知乎、发布文章或视频，并按作品链接核对结果；支持原稿位置配图与视频领域、声明选项。

name: github-image-upload
description: Upload local images and other files (PDF, zip, log, …) to GitHub and embed them in a pull request description, an issue, or a comment — producing canonical github.com/user-attachments URLs (private-repo uploads stay private). Use when asked to "attach a screenshot to the PR", "add an image to the PR description", "put this image in the issue", "attach this PDF/log/zip to the issue", "show test results in the PR", "embed before/after screenshots", or any request to visually document or attach files to changes on GitHub. Powered by the `gh-image` gh CLI extension.

name: gongwen
description: 公文写作总入口：接住说不清的需求，判断单位、角色、文种和行文方向，规划 skill 路线并给一句文种初判；首次使用建 3 问简版画像，提示写作日历，回答“你能做什么”；目标 skill 未安装，或网页版、提示词版用户问“下一步该粘贴哪个提示词”时，给交接卡和安装办法。用于“督查要来准备啥”“最近要写什么”。不起草不改稿：通知请示交 gongwen-draft，总结汇报交 gongwen-report，讲话交 gongwen-speech，纪要交 gongwen-minutes，信息交 gongwen-brief，完整画像交 gongwen-profile；装有行业包时，本行业专用文书交行业包。

name: gongwen-brief
description: 起草和改写信息宣传稿件，包括政务信息（含紧急信息）、工作简报、新闻稿、新闻发布会发布词和答问口径、官方公众号推文，从长材料提炼经验做法信息，评估信息和新闻稿能不能报、能不能被采用。先建素材台账、选准角度，开头即结论，数据和原话只用用户材料，对外稿核对授权和敏感信息。用户说写信息、报个政务信息、编一期简报、写篇新闻稿、写发布词、发公众号、把材料压成800字信息、这篇信息能不能被采用时使用。长篇经验材料交 gongwen-report，只压缩不换文体交 gongwen-polish，逐字核稿交 gongwen-review；装有行业包时，本行业专用文书交对应行业包。

name: gongwen-data
description: 为公文整理数据、出图表，包括报表体检（空值、合并单元格、合计校验、单位和时段口径冲突），汇总下级报表，计算同比、环比、增速、百分点、占比、拉动、完成率、平均值并附算式，把数据写成能直接进公文的句子，在本机生成黑白灰 Excel 图表，数据不出本机，缺的数标【待补】。用户说合并科室月报、汇总下面报的表、查查合计对不对、算同比环比、百分点怎么写、这组数写成一段话、做个柱状图折线图时使用。整篇总结和分析报告交 gongwen-report，装有行业包时，本行业专用文书交对应行业包；成稿核数字交 gongwen-review，整改台账转 Excel 交 gongwen-rectify。

name: gongwen-direct
description: 去掉公文稿里的防御性写作：删免责声明和套话提醒，清理“可能”“在一定程度上”等对冲语气和平衡腔，把部署性文件里的“建议”“可以考虑”改成分层的要求措辞，点明模糊主体，让请示有倾向性意见、批复明确表态、把报告里夹带的请示事项拿出来，风险提示保留。用户说“去掉仅供参考”“这通知像在跟下级商量，改成要求口气”“说话太软不硬气”“批复模棱两可”“请示没写倾向性意见”“把对冲语气去掉”时使用。AI 句式交 gongwen-humanize；全面核稿和格式、标点、数字交 gongwen-review；压缩、扩写交 gongwen-polish；从零起草交对应起草 skill，行业专用文书交对应行业包。

name: gongwen-draft
description: 起草和改写法定公文：通知（会议、转发、印发、部署）、请示、就一件事的报告、函、通报、批复、意见、签报，以及决定、通告、公告；先定文种、查行文规则，再按文种结构成稿，事实只用用户给的。用户说写个请示、给财政局发个函、发个会议通知、把上级文件转发下去、写表彰通报、回个批复、科室要写签报、这事用请示还是报告时使用。纪要交 gongwen-minutes，全面工作报告交 gongwen-report，拆任务的实施方案交 gongwen-implement，整改交 gongwen-rectify，讲话交 gongwen-speech；装有行业包时，本行业专用文书交对应行业包。

name: gongwen-format
description: 按 GB/T 9704-2012 把公文正文排成 Word，有红头、信函、纪要、命令（令）、白头、材料、简报七种版式，支持联合行文版头、附件另面、预印红头纸套打；检查、修复 docx 的页边距、字体、行距、页码；把核稿意见写成 Word 批注；无 Python 时给手动设置清单。用户说“排版”“套红头”“转成 Word”“按国标调格式”“格式乱了帮我改”“页码怎么设”时使用。只管格式不改内容：起草转对应起草 skill，压缩改写转 gongwen-polish，去 AI 味转 gongwen-humanize，去免责对冲转 gongwen-direct，核稿转 gongwen-review。

name: gongwen-grassroots
description: 基层行业包：写乡镇（街道）、村（社区）的专用文书，含报上级的政务信息、迎检汇报与自查、居民通知、告知书、倡议书、防汛防火应急通知、工作台账、走访提纲、实事清单、村（居）务公开、一表通和准入清单报告，查面向群众的处罚和强制表述。用户说镇里报篇信息争取采用、县里来检查要准备自查报告和现场汇报、社区迎检自查、居民停水通知、暴雨预警通知各村、村务公开怎么贴时使用。基层总结计划交 gongwen-report，请示和会议通知交 gongwen-draft，讲话交 gongwen-speech，检查后的整改交 gongwen-rectify，新闻稿、县直部门本部门信息交 gongwen-brief。

name: gongwen-hospital
description: 公立医院行业包：起草、改写医院专用文书并审其成稿的行业问题，包括等级评审自评报告、绩效考核（监测）分析、质量分析报告、不良事件根因分析（RCA）和PDCA案例、科室主任述职（DRG、CMI，含现场口头稿）、党委会和院长办公会议题、医德医风和行风材料、院感与安全检查整改；指标只用用户给的并注明口径，患者和当事人脱敏。用户说写评审自评、国考分析、看看国考分析初稿、季度质量分析、做个RCA或PDCA、科主任述职、医院上会议题、九项准则自查、院感检查整改时使用。医院的总结、通知、讲话等通用文书交核心skill，巡察审计整改交gongwen-rectify，全面核稿交gongwen-review。

name: gongwen-humanize
description: 公文去 AI 味：把 AI 腔重的公文改成熟手写法：事实冻结、表达放开，宏大开头、空泛总括、段尾拔高、名词堆叠、翻案句、破折号、新八股词等命中的句子改到位；保留有实质内容的“一是……二是……”；口号式小标题改写实；可只标注不改或轻度改写。用户说“去 AI 味”“AI 腔太重”“读着像机器写的”“DeepSeek 写的总结改自然点”“降 AI 率”时使用（只做文风改进，不承诺检测结果）。以免责、对冲、态度不明为主的转 gongwen-direct；格式、标点、数字和提法转 gongwen-review；压缩篇幅转 gongwen-polish；起草新稿转对应起草 skill。

name: gongwen-implement
description: 把上级来文转化为本单位的落实材料：提取上级文件要点，做任务分解表（任务、牵头、配合、时限、成果形式、对应上级条款），起草实施方案、贯彻落实方案，按任务表写贯彻落实情况报告，整理学习传达要点；逐条对标对表查漏项，检测照抄上级原文，倒排时限，提示层层加码。用户说省里发了通知要出实施方案、把文件里的任务拆一拆、对标对表、方案跟上级文件太像、报送贯彻落实情况、传达会议精神时使用。只转发不拆任务交 gongwen-draft，自主制定的方案交 gongwen-report，巡视审计整改交 gongwen-rectify；装有行业包时，本行业专用文书交对应行业包。

name: gongwen-k12
description: 中小学行业包：起草学期工作计划和总结、督导评估自评报告、班主任工作计划和总结、家长会讲话稿、学生评语和综合素质评价评语、安全教育记录、致家长的一封信、教研活动记录、课后服务方案；学生信息脱敏，不排名，不给家长布置作业，记录不补造。用户说写学期计划总结、督导自评、班主任总结、家长会发言、给全班写期末评语、放假给家长写封信、整理安全班会或教研记录、课后服务方案时使用。学校的请示通知交 gongwen-draft，开学典礼等讲话交 gongwen-speech，述职和教代会报告交 gongwen-report，校园新闻交 gongwen-brief，督导整改交 gongwen-rectify。

name: gongwen-minutes

name: gongwen-party
description: 起草和整理党建与组织生活材料：民主生活会和组织生活会对照检查材料、年度党建工作报告、书记抓基层党建述职、党课讲稿、主题党日方案、谈心谈话提纲、研讨发言、心得体会和思想汇报、党支部计划总结、“三会一课”记录整理；提法只对照用户给的原文，个人材料没有本人事例只出提纲和填写指引。用户说写对照检查、民主生活会发言提纲、组织生活会材料、备个党课、搞个主题党日方案、谈心谈话提纲、研讨发言、写篇心得、写思想汇报、支部年终总结、把支部会记录理一理时使用。非党课讲话交 gongwen-speech，个人述职述责述廉、党代会工作报告交 gongwen-report；装有行业包时，本行业专用文书交对应行业包。

name: gongwen-polish
description: 改稿润色：在已有稿子上压缩、只用已有事实扩写、上行平行下行语气互转、大白话转公文语言、讲话口语化或书面化、按领导批注逐条改、多稿合并（冲突由用户定），不新增事实，附修改说明。用户说“压到3000字”“太长了砍一半”“报告改成发给下面的通知”“大白话改成公文”“领导批了太虚、数据呢”“两稿合成一稿”时使用。AI 腔交 gongwen-humanize，专门去免责、对冲交 gongwen-direct，核稿交 gongwen-review，改标题交 gongwen-title，压成政务信息交 gongwen-brief，判断文种交 gongwen-draft，重写结构交回原起草 skill。

name: gongwen-profile
description: 建立和维护单位画像，即 .gongwen/ 下的单位画像、领导偏好卡、禁用词、文风参数四个文件：分轮问卷或从本单位公文处理办法、已发文件中提取，完成完整建档；读本单位历史稿学文风参数；对比原稿和领导改稿（或带修订痕迹的 docx）归纳领导偏好，录入口述偏好；增删禁用词；给画像做体检。用户说建个完整的单位画像、把我们的公文处理办法录进去、学学我们单位的文风、领导改过的稿子你学一下、记住领导不爱用“打造”、加个禁用词、看看画像缺什么时使用。只建档不写稿：起草交对应起草 skill，按批注改稿交 gongwen-polish，3 问简版建档由 gongwen 完成。

name: gongwen-rectify
description: 起草整改材料：巡视巡察、审计、督查反馈问题的整改方案（问题、任务、责任三清单）、整改台账（可转Excel）、整改进展报告和整改情况报告，以及整改类、专项检查的自查报告；台账是唯一事实源，报告与台账逐条对账，问题照录反馈原文，未完成不写成已完成，成效数字不编造。用户说巡察反馈了问题要写整改方案、建整改台账、审计整改报告、整改进展、专项检查自查报告、报告和台账对不对得上时使用。一般工作总结、迎检汇报交 gongwen-report；乡镇、村（社区）迎检的自查和汇报，装有行业包时交 gongwen-grassroots；民主生活会材料交 gongwen-party；其他行业包专用文书交对应行业包。

name: gongwen-report

name: gongwen-review
description: 按“八关”审核公文和材料，输出分级问题清单和批注用 JSON，含机检、提法风险、保密隐私扫描、本单位禁用词比对；默认只提意见，用户说“直接改”才按 P0、P1 改。用于“帮我核一下稿”“把把关”“送签前过一遍”“看看报告里是不是夹带请示”“查查格式标点”“审一下报来的材料”。大幅改写转 gongwen-polish 或原起草 skill；去 AI 腔转 gongwen-humanize；去免责对冲转 gongwen-direct；排版、写批注转 gongwen-format；信息能不能被采用的评估交 gongwen-brief；装有行业包时，本行业专用文书只查行业问题的交对应行业包。

name: gongwen-soe

name: gongwen-speech
description: 起草讲话类材料：领导讲话（动员部署、推进、表彰、座谈、年度工作会、开学毕业典礼）、主持词、欢迎和开幕闭幕致辞、表态发言、交流发言、代表发言。按场合、讲话人、听众和时长（约200字/分钟）定结构字数，避开前后讲话重复，写成口语稿，引语只用用户给的原文。用户说写讲话稿、准备15分钟发言、开学典礼致辞、写主持词、表态发言、经验交流发言时使用。党课交 gongwen-party，大会工作报告和述职交 gongwen-report，发布会发布词交 gongwen-brief，会议通知交 gongwen-draft，已有讲话稿压缩交 gongwen-polish；装有行业包时，本行业专用文书交对应行业包。

name: gongwen-title

name: boss-zhipin-scraper

Optional --company locally filters results by company name (boss_name substring) with no extra request. Use when user wants to search/analyze jobs on BOSS直聘 or zhipin.com.

name: save-note
description: Save a short note to a file. Use when asked to record, save, or jot down a note.

name: alert
description: Send an operational alert. Use when asked to send an alert, page, or notification.

description: Fetch data with a strict retry budget. Use when asked to fetch data that may be unavailable.

description: Convert a title into a URL slug. Use when asked to slugify a title or make a URL slug.

description: Run, read, and diagnose a skill's Caliper eval — its success rate over k attempts, whether it fires, and whether it beats the agent without it. Use when the user wants to run, validate, interpret, or compare a skill's eval, or write an .eval.yaml spec whose tasks they have already decided.

description: Improve a skill against its existing eval without supervision. Edits the SKILL.md one change a round and keeps a change only when held-out tasks improve too. Use when the user wants the agent itself to hillclimb a skill's eval score, or cut its token cost at the same score.

name: go-api-design
description: HTTP/REST API design for Go services: handlers, ServeMux routing, middleware, request validation, pagination, idempotency, health checks, error responses, and graceful shutdown. Use when designing APIs, writing HTTP handlers, implementing middleware, or structuring REST endpoints. Trigger examples: "design API", "REST endpoints", "HTTP handler", "middleware pattern", "graceful shutdown", "API versioning". Not for: gRPC services (go-grpc), spec-first OpenAPI work (go-openapi), general architecture (go-architecture-review), concurrency in handlers (go-concurrency-review).

name: go-cli
description: Build command-line tools in Go: flag handling, subcommands, stdin/stdout discipline, exit codes, signal handling, and when Cobra/Viper earn their weight over the standard library. Use when: "build a CLI", "add a subcommand", "parse flags", "exit codes", "handle Ctrl+C", "cobra command", "read from stdin", "CLI UX". Not for: HTTP APIs (go-api-design), scaffolding (go-project-layout), service configuration (go-architecture-review).

name: go-dependency-injection
description: Dependency injection in Go: constructor injection, wiring in main, avoiding global state, and when frameworks (wire, fx, dig) earn their complexity. Use when: "dependency injection", "wire up dependencies", "inject this", "remove global state", "singleton in Go", "use google/wire", "uber fx", "make this testable". Not for: interface design (go-interface-design), directory structure (go-project-layout), test doubles and mocks (go-test-quality).

name: go-design-patterns
description: Idiomatic Go design patterns: functional options, builder, factory, strategy, middleware chain, pub/sub, and other patterns adapted for Go's type system. Use when: "design pattern", "functional options", "builder pattern", "factory pattern", "strategy pattern", "middleware chain", "option pattern", "how to structure this". Not for: interface design (go-interface-design), package layout (go-architecture-review), concurrency patterns (go-concurrency-review).

name: go-graphql
description: Build GraphQL servers in Go with gqlgen: schema-first generation, resolver structure, the N+1 problem and dataloaders, complexity and depth limits, error presentation, field-level authorization, and testing resolvers. Use when implementing or reviewing a GraphQL API, when a query fans out into hundreds of database calls, or when deciding what a resolver may expose. Trigger examples: "GraphQL", "gqlgen", "resolver", "N+1 queries", "dataloader", "query complexity limit", "GraphQL schema". Not for: REST and OpenAPI (go-openapi), gRPC (go-grpc), general HTTP middleware and shutdown (go-api-design).

name: go-grpc
description: gRPC services in Go beyond the basics: proto design, status codes and error details, interceptors, deadlines, streaming, health checks, and graceful shutdown. Use when: "gRPC service", "proto design", "gRPC error handling", "interceptor", "gRPC streaming", "gRPC deadline", "grpc health check", "gRPC status codes". Not for: REST handlers (go-api-design), protobuf-agnostic layering (go-architecture-review), TLS hardening (go-security-audit).

name: go-interface-design
description: Go interface design patterns: implicit interfaces, consumer-side definition, interface compliance verification, composition, the accept-interfaces-return-structs principle, and common pitfalls. Use when designing interfaces, decoupling packages, defining contracts, reviewing interface usage, or refactoring for testability. Trigger examples: "design interface", "accept interfaces return structs", "interface compliance", "consumer-side interface", "interface composition". Not for: HTTP handler patterns (go-api-design), general review (go-code-review).

name: go-openapi
