Use this skill when the user wants to upload audience members, remove specific users, or clear/replace an entire audience for Customer Match, mobile device ID audiences, or any other audience use case supported by the Data Manager API. Don't use for uploading events or conversions (use the data-manager-api-event-ingestion skill).

name: data-manager-api-event-ingestion
description: Guides developers through implementing event and conversion ingestion to Google products using the Data Manager API /v1/events/ingest endpoint and its associated client libraries. Use this skill when the user wants to upload offline conversions, enhanced conversions for leads, click conversions, Google Analytics web or app events, or any other event ingestion use case supported by the Data Manager API. Don't use for uploading audience members (use the data-manager-api-audience-ingestion skill).

name: data-manager-api-setup
description: Guides developers through client library installation and authentication setup steps for the Data Manager API. Use this skill when a user is getting started with the Data Manager API and needs to setup their local environment, install the client library, or setup access to the API. Don't use for implementing audience or event ingestion logic (use the data-manager-api-audience-ingestion or data-manager-api-event-ingestion skills instead).

name: google-ads-api-account-diagnostics
description: Diagnoses Google Ads account performance issues such as conversion loss (value or volume), low lead flow/volume, and lost impression share (opportunities) due to ad rank, bids, or budgets. Use when troubleshooting sudden performance drops, analyzing campaign impression share metrics, investigating low lead flow, or searching for bidding and budget constraints. Don't use for setting up new campaigns, uploading conversion events directly, or general Google Mobile Ads SDK integration issues (use gma-android-integrate instead).

name: google-ads-api-mcp-setup
description: Guides developers through downloading, configuring, and installing the official open-source Google Ads MCP Server. Use this skill when a user wants to connect their AI assistant (such as Gemini, Claude Code, or Cursor) to their Google Ads account to query campaigns or retrieve reporting metrics using natural language.

name: google-ads-api-quickstart
description: Guides developers through Google Ads API quickstart: credential setup, choosing from 6 client libraries/REST, configuring environments, and running a "retrieve campaigns" script. Troubleshoots common setup errors: USER_PERMISSION_DENIED, login_customer_id issues, and CLOUD_PROJECT_NOT_APPROVED_FOR_PRODUCTION (a Google Cloud project with Test access calling a production account). Use this skill when: - The user asks how to get started with the Google Ads API. - The user needs to set up Google Ads API access in a Google Cloud project or OAuth credentials. - The user wants to write a quickstart/example script for Google Ads. - The user encounters errors like USER_PERMISSION_DENIED, CLOUD_PROJECT_NOT_APPROVED_FOR_PRODUCTION, or the legacy DEVELOPER_TOKEN_NOT_APPROVED.

name: google-mobile-ads-android-migrate-to-next-gen
description: Migrates Android applications from the old, legacy Google Mobile Ads (GMA) SDK (com.google.android.gms:play-services-ads) to the new GMA Next-Gen SDK (com.google.android.libraries.ads.mobile.sdk:ads-mobile-sdk). Provides comprehensive mapping tables for imports, classes, and method signatures to help determine migration steps. Use when migrating an existing Android codebase from the old, legacy GMA SDK to GMA Next-Gen SDK.

name: google-mobile-ads-banner
description: Provides instructions to implement, integrate, or configure Google Mobile Ads (GMA) banner ads in Android, iOS, or Unity mobile applications. Use when the task involves setting up banner ads in a mobile application. Don't use for other ad formats like interstitial or rewarded ads.

name: google-mobile-ads-get-started
description: Provides instructions for integrating the Google Mobile Ads (GMA) SDK. Use this skill when the user wants to get started with, install, integrate, set up, or configure the SDK for AdMob or Ad Manager, GMA Next-Gen SDK or mobile ads framework in an Android, iOS, or Unity application.

name: google-mobile-ads-interstitial
description: Provides instructions for implementing, integrating, or configuring Google Mobile Ads (GMA) SDK interstitial ads in Android, iOS, or Unity mobile applications. Use when the task involves setting up interstitial ads. Don't use for "rewarded interstitial" ads.

name: google-mobile-ads-rewarded
description: Provides instructions for implementing, integrating, or configuring Google Mobile Ads (GMA) SDK rewarded ads in Android, iOS, or Unity mobile applications. Use when the task involves setting up rewarded ads. Don't use for "rewarded interstitial" ads.

name: google-mobile-ads-validate
description: Validates a project's Google Mobile Ads (GMA) SDK integration for iOS, Android, or Unity projects. Use when conducting a full pre-launch audit of an app that integrates GMA SDK or when validating any individual GMA SDK integration checks, such as when validating ad unit IDs and ad formats, SKAdNetwork IDs, mediation adapter SDK version compatibility, or ad preloading.

name: ima-dai-sdk
description: Integrates the Google Interactive Media Ads (IMA) Dynamic Ad Insertion (DAI) SDK into websites, web apps, mobile apps, or TV apps. Use when: - A video player needs to load and play HLS or DASH streams in web apps, Android apps, iOS apps, tvOS apps, Cast (CAF) receivers, or Roku channels. - The app needs to make use of a Google DAI livestream event asset key, or content source CMS ID, video ID for video on demand. Don't use this skill to load and play a VAST or VMAP URL.

name: ima-sdk-client-side
description: Supports Interactive Media Ads (IMA) SDK. Use this skill for client-side ad insertion when you are requesting video ads for websites, apps, TVs or other platforms using VAST or VMAP. Do not use for Dynamic Ad Insertion (DAI), SSAI, or SGAI.

name: google-analytics-admin-api-basics
description: Manages Google Analytics account and property settings, enables the Analytics Admin API via the Cloud CLI, lists accounts and properties, and manages data streams, custom dimensions, conversion events, and integrations. Use when you need to programmatically configure Google Analytics accounts, provision properties, manage data retention, configure Measurement Protocol secrets, or manage Firebase and Google Ads links.

name: google-analytics-data-api-basics
description: Manages Google Analytics reporting data, enables the Analytics Data API via the Cloud CLI, and creates reports using the Google Analytics Data API (v1beta). Use when you need to interact with Google Analytics properties, run customized analytics reports, query metrics (like activeUsers, screenPageViews) and dimensions (like city, date), check metrics and dimensions compatibility, or verify API enablement. Don't use for Google Analytics Admin API operations (e.g., creating properties, managing users) or for front-end tracking installation.

name: agent-platform-access-audit
description: Audits AI agent data access, blast radius, and blocked policy operations in Google Cloud by querying Cloud Audit Logs via BigQuery. Use when investigating what resources or services an agent accessed, identifying top originating principals the agent is acting as, or triaging PERMISSION_DENIED errors to distinguish VPC Service Controls perimeter violations from IAM permission denials. Don't use for configuring Cloud Monitoring alert policies, modifying IAM policies or VPC Service Controls perimeters, querying non-audit application logs, or performing write operations.

name: agent-platform-alert-configuration
description: Configures best-practice alerting policies for AI agents using OpenTelemetry (OTel) metrics, generating output as Terraform (.tf) configuration files. Use when analyzing, writing, or deploying alerting policies to monitor agent latency, error rates, token usage, and quality metrics. Don't use for standard infrastructure monitoring unrelated to AI agents, or when the agent is not instrumented with OpenTelemetry (for Reliability, Cost, Safety, Security alerts). NOTE: Reliability, Cost, Safety, and Security alerts use generic OTel metrics and work across runtimes (such as Cloud Run, Vertex AI). Quality alerts rely on Vertex AI Online Monitors and are strictly bound to Vertex AI deployments.

name: agent-platform-architecture
description: Designs, engineers, and validates enterprise Gemini platform architectures. Use when designing multi-project hierarchies (Host, Central Governance Hub, Runtime Spoke, Tool/MCP Spoke), configuring Agent Gateway, authoring Agent Connectivity Templates (ALL_TRAFFIC vs PRIVATE_RANGES_ONLY), deploying Secure Web Proxy (SWP) with Policy-Based Routing (PBR) or Cross-Cloud mTLS Egress Hubs, configuring Private CA TrustConfig with Internal ALB + Serverless NEG, implementing Unified Access Policies (UAP Policy V2 CEL) and Semantic Governance (SGP), configuring 3P IdP Token Exchange (EntraID/Ping/Okta via ext_proc + STS) or Agent Identity Auth Manager (SPIFFE), enforcing Model Armor Floor Settings and Fail-Closed guardrails, deploying Cross-Project Registry sync, binding ADK agents on Agent Runtime, or executing Day-2 lifecycle operations. Don't use for read-only live log triage or incident diagnosis, or generic Google Cloud Identity and Access Management (IAM) debugging.

name: agent-platform-autorater-customization
description: Customizes an autorater (evaluation metric) for an AI agent so its grades match the user's own judgment, starting from the agent's real trajectories. Use when a user wants a metric tailored to their agent, wants to turn failing trajectories into rubrics, says an existing autorater grades their agent wrong, or wants an autorater to agree with human labels (autorater hillclimbing, judge calibration). Don't use for quick evals with built-in metrics or for improving the agent itself (use agent-platform-eval-flywheel).

name: agent-platform-deploy
description: Deploy open models or custom weights from Model Garden to Agent Platform endpoints, check the status of an in-progress deployment operation, or clean up resources by undeploying models and deleting endpoints. Use when asked to actively deploy a model, list the Model Garden CATALOG of available models, check if a specific model is deployable (`gcloud ai model-garden models list-deployment-config`), query deployment cost, troubleshoot deployment errors (like quota limits), or undeploy/clean up endpoints. Also use when copying and deploying a 1P Tuned Model. Don't use for pure listing/discovery questions of the form "is X deployed?", "list my endpoints", or "which regions have models running?" — for those use `agent-platform-endpoint-management`. Don't use for running model evaluations (use `agent-platform-eval-flywheel` skill).

name: agent-platform-endpoint-management
description: Manages Agent Platform serving endpoints. Use when you need to create, list, describe, update, or delete serving endpoints for model deployment on Agent Platform. Also use when troubleshooting endpoint permission, quota, or resource busy errors. Don't use for deploying models to endpoints or for running model evaluations.

name: agent-platform-eval-flywheel
description: Measures and improves the quality of AI models and agents on Google Cloud using the Eval Quality Flywheel methodology. Use when generating synthetic user scenarios, evaluating an agent or model, building an eval dataset, picking or writing evaluation metrics, analyzing failures, comparing results before and after a fix, or when guidance is needed on Agent Platform eval methodology — including dataset schema, LLM-as-judge scoring, and common failure causes. For fine-tuning, use agent-platform-tuning. For general production deployment, use agent-platform-deploy.

name: agent-platform-inference
description: Connects to and performs inference with Google Cloud Agent Platform GenAI models, including First-Party Gemini models and Third-Party OpenMaaS models (Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen, etc.). Use when asked to perform inference, ask a model a question, run a test prompt, execute chat completions, or generate code for calling Gemini or OpenMaaS models, authenticate with GenAI SDK, OpenAI SDK, or legacy Agent Platform SDK, configure base URLs and global/regional endpoints, or troubleshoot 429 Resource Exhausted (DSQ), 400 User Validation, or 404 Not Found errors. Don't use for deploying models to endpoints or for running model evaluations.

name: agent-platform-migrate-from-ai-studio
description: Guides agents and users through migrating from Gemini API in Google AI Studio to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI). Use this skill when moving applications to Google Cloud, to leverage Cloud credits, or to unify inferencing with other Cloud infrastructure (IAM, billing, telemetry).

name: agent-platform-model-registry
description: Agent Platform Model Registry Management. Use when you need to upload, list, describe, update, or delete machine learning models (and their versions) in the Agent Platform Model Registry. Don't use for model training, model deployment to endpoints, or managing non-Agent Platform models.

name: agent-platform-prompt-management
description: Manages and orchestrates prompts in Agent Platform. Use when you need to create, list, retrieve, version, or delete managed prompts in Agent Platform. Don't use for model training, model deployment to endpoints, or managing non-Agent Platform prompts.

name: agent-platform-rag-engine-management
description: Manage and query Agent Platform RAG Engine Corpora and retrieve grounded contexts using the Google GenAI SDK. Use when listing RAG corpora or files, inspecting a corpus, retrieving contexts, or generating content grounded in a RAG corpus. Do not use for standard database queries (use SQL/Spanner skills), Google Workspace RAG, or other RAG products like gRAG.

name: agent-platform-skill-registry
description: Interact with the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Skill Registry to create and search for available skills. Use this skill to enable agents to register functionality or discover new capabilities.

name: agent-platform-troubleshooting
description: Troubleshoots Google Cloud Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform issues across Agent Gateway, Agent Connectivity Templates (ACT), Agent Registry, Agent Identity, Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP), Unified Access Policies (UAP), Model Armor, Semantic Governance Policies (SGP), Cloud DNS peering, Private CA TrustConfig, Next-Hop Secure Web Proxy (SWP), Explicit HTTPS Proxy (L4 AuthzPolicy), and Cloud Trace. Use when agent requests fail with 401/403/404/498/500/503 or Code 13, Egress request is not authorized, HTTP CONNECT fails with 404, Agent Runtime crashes on startup, or gateway/ACT/IAP/Model Armor/SGP configs fail validation. Don't use for general Google Cloud Identity and Access Management (IAM) debugging or networking issues unrelated to the Agent Platform stack.

name: agent-platform-tuning
description: Agent Platform Model Tuning. Use when you need to fine-tune open models or Gemini models using Agent Platform infrastructure. Don't use for model training outside Agent Platform, model deployment to endpoints (use `agent-platform-deploy`), or managing serving endpoints (use `agent-platform-endpoint-management`).

name: agent-platform-tuning-management
description: Manages GenAI tuning jobs in Agent Platform. Use this to list, get, or cancel ongoing model tuning jobs. Don't use for fine-tuning models (use `agent-platform-tuning`), deploying models to endpoints (use `agent-platform-deploy`), or managing serving endpoints (use `agent-platform-endpoint-management`).

name: alloydb-basics
description: Manages clusters, instances, and backups for AlloyDB for PostgreSQL, and integrates with AlloyDB Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools for automated database operations. Use when creating, configuring, or administering AlloyDB databases. Do NOT use for general PostgreSQL instances (e.g. Cloud SQL) or other GCP databases.

name: api-gateway-backend-security-and-rate-limiting
description: Secures and rate limits backend services behind Google Cloud API Gateway across OpenAPI 2.0 and OpenAPI 3.0.x API configurations, including MCP-enabled gateways. Use when configuring API key or JWT authentication, locking down Cloud Run or Cloud Run functions backends with a gateway service account, reading authenticated claims from X-Apigateway-Api-Userinfo, setting per-project request quotas, or diagnosing HTTP 429 and HTTP 500 Service Control Quota errors. Do not use for Apigee, GKE Gateway API, Cloud Load Balancing custom domain setup, or LLM model routing.

name: api-gateway-mcp-server
description: Configures Google Cloud API Gateway to act as a remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server (Public Preview) that exposes REST APIs as agent tools over HTTP (POST /mcp). Use when migrating OpenAPI 2.0 specs to OpenAPI 3.x for MCP, annotating specs with x-google-api-management.mcp and x-google-mcp-tool, securing tools/list with JWTs or API keys, connecting Google ADK (McpToolset) or Apigee API hub and Agent Registry, or troubleshooting MCP JSON-RPC errors (-32601, -32602, -32000). Do not use for Apigee X proxy bundles, outbound LLM model routing, or GKE Gateway API.

name: api-gateway-openapi-spec-authoring
description: Writes, migrates, and fixes OpenAPI specs for Google Cloud API Gateway. Use when converting an OpenAPI 2.0 (Swagger) spec to OpenAPI 3.x, writing a new OpenAPI 3.x spec, or fixing a failed "gcloud api-gateway api-configs create", such as "extension is only supported in OpenAPI 2.x". Also use when quotas set with x-google-quota are never enforced, or when a backend receives path parameters as query parameters. Don't use for adding or debugging MCP tools (use api-gateway-mcp-server), backend lockdown or HTTP 429 tuning (use api-gateway-backend-security-and-rate-limiting), Cloud Endpoints, Apigee, or GKE Gateway API.

name: api-gateway-troubleshooting
description: Diagnoses failing requests and deployment errors on Google Cloud API Gateway. Use when calls through a gateway return 4xx or 5xx errors, including 429 and other quota errors, time out, or fail a CORS preflight; when `api-configs create` fails with a service account, concurrency, or limit error, or `gateways create` or `gateways update` fails; when a custom domain, load balancer, or TLS finding involves a gateway; or when the user asks if Google is at fault. Don't use for Apigee, Cloud Endpoints, or GKE Gateway API. For OpenAPI errors from `api-configs create`, use api-gateway-openapi-spec-authoring; for setting up or changing API keys, JWTs, or quotas, use api-gateway-backend-security-and-rate-limiting; for MCP `/mcp` errors, use api-gateway-mcp-server.

name: apigee-agent-gateway-governance
description: Stands up an Apigee API proxy that a Google Cloud Agent Gateway calls as an ext-proc (Service Extension) callout on an agent's LLM traffic, to meter token usage per model, extract caller identity, and apply Model Armor prompt screening or a semantic cache. Use when wiring Apigee in as an AI gateway behind an Agent Gateway, when an agent's model egress needs governing, or when a callout proxy returns no verdict and you need to find out why. The distinguishing question is whether Apigee forwards the traffic or only inspects it: this skill is inspect-only, and builds the proxy itself. Don't use it when Apigee is meant to receive a request and route it onward to a backend — including hosting an MCP server behind Apigee — which needs a proxy with a target instead. Don't use for governing the agent's calls to tools or MCP servers. Don't use for choosing or switching which model a request goes to. Don't use for creating the Agent Gateway itself, nor for Apigee hybrid.

name: application-design-center-design-deploy
description: Processes GCP infrastructure design and deployment workflows within Application Design Center (ADC). Use when: - Designing GCP infrastructure with Terraform. - Validating local HCL. - Performing best-practice plan scans. - Importing templates to Application Design Center (ADC). - Deploying templates. - Troubleshooting deployment failures. Boundaries: - Only use for GCP-specific cloud infrastructure. - Only use for Terraform coding within the ADC context.

name: application-integration-authoring
description: Builds, versions, publishes, tests, and executes Google Cloud Application Integration workflows through the REST API and Python discovery client, and promotes versions across environments. Use when listing integrations, downloading or uploading integration versions as JSON, configuring API triggers or config variables, publishing drafts, invoking integrations, or automating CI/CD promotion. Do not use for initial region provisioning and IAM setup (use application-integration-basics) or diagnosing failed runs and logs (use application-integration-troubleshooting).

name: application-integration-basics
description: Explains Google Cloud Application Integration concepts, region provisioning, IAM roles, run-as service accounts, interface choices (REST, Python discovery client, Terraform, ADK), and platform limits. Use when setting up Application Integration in a Google Cloud project, enabling required APIs, provisioning a region, configuring IAM or run-as service accounts, choosing between Application Integration and custom code, or checking quotas and timeouts. Do not use for building, publishing, or invoking integrations (use application-integration-authoring) or diagnosing failed or stuck runs and logs (use application-integration-troubleshooting).

name: application-integration-troubleshooting
description: Diagnoses failed, stuck, or silent Google Cloud Application Integration runs and Integration Connectors tasks using the REST API, Cloud Logging, and Cloud Monitoring. Use when an integration fails, returns HTTP 200 without doing the expected work, hangs in a suspended or retry state, or hits IAM, run-as service account, connector health, or quota errors. Do not use for initial region provisioning (use application-integration-basics) or building and deploying versions (use application-integration-authoring).

name: assured-workloads-basics
description: Provisions, inspects, updates, and deletes Google Cloud Assured Workloads V1 compliant folders, CMEK settings, Sovereign Controls by Partners, and service usage restrictions. Use when creating, listing, describing, updating, or deleting an Assured Workloads workload for any compliance regime or data boundary (FedRAMP, DoD IL2/IL4/IL5, ITAR, CJIS, Healthcare, Sovereign Controls by Partners, or Regional Data Boundaries). Don't use for brownfield assessments or custom frameworks (use assuredworkloads-environment-assessor or assuredworkloads-frameworks-*), or non-compliant folders.

name: assuredworkloads-environment-assessor
description: Discover Google Cloud resource telemetry and effective Org Policies, evaluate brownfield workloads against sovereign data boundary and compliance standards (EU Data Boundary with Support, FedRAMP Moderate/High, DoD IL4/IL5, ITAR, CJIS, US/EU Regional Data Boundaries), and recommend the optimal Assured Workloads Framework. Use when asked to: "assess my environment for compliance", "which Assured Workloads framework should I use?", "check if my folder is ready for EU sovereignty", "evaluate compliance posture for folders/123 or projects/xyz", or "discover compliance gaps before deployment". Do NOT use for live mutating policy deployments, generating deep audit reports via Cloud Audit Manager, generating remediation scripts, or authoring custom Assured Workloads frameworks.

name: assuredworkloads-frameworks-author
description: Authors custom cloud controls and customized frameworks for Assured Workloads when built-in resources cannot satisfy core requirements. Use when creating or synthesizing custom data boundary resources. Don't use for browsing or mapping existing built-in frameworks (use assuredworkloads-frameworks-navigator instead).

name: assuredworkloads-frameworks-navigator
description: Acts as a Data Boundary Compliance Analyst that maps user compliance queries against Data Boundary Frameworks and cloud controls, validates matched resources, and recommends appropriate Frameworks or cloud controls. Use when mapping direct natural language workload requirements to Assured Workloads / Data Boundary Frameworks and cloud controls, browsing built-in Data Boundary frameworks, or identifying major requirement gaps. Don't use for non-Data-Boundary Compliance Manager posture assessments or direct Terraform deployment execution without framework selection.

name: bigquery-ai-ml
description: Leverages BigQuery's built-in machine learning and GenAI capabilities for advanced data analytics. Use when you need to write SQL queries that perform time-series forecasting, predict values, detect outliers or anomalies, find key drivers, perform semantic search or vector search, classify text, calculate similarity, summarize content, translate language, evaluate models, filter by semantic conditions, measure the causal effect of an intervention, compute correlations between columns, generate descriptive statistics and table distribution profiles, detect change points or structural breaks, extract trend or seasonality components, or leverage generative AI capabilities in BigQuery. Do not use for general BigQuery dataset, table, or job management requests.

name: bigquery-basics
description: Manages datasets, tables, and jobs in BigQuery. Use when you need to interact with BigQuery, run SQL queries, manage BigQuery resources (datasets, tables, views), or perform basic data ingestion and analysis.

name: bigquery-bigframes
description: Generates Python code using BigQuery DataFrames (BigFrames). Use by default for any Python data task involving BigQuery, including data processing, analysis, and machine learning. Don't use for SQL-first workflows or the google-cloud-bigquery client library — use bigquery-basics.

name: bigquery-migration-data-loader
description: Provisions BigQuery datasets, ingests staged Parquet files directly into native BigQuery tables by using bq load, and deploys already-translated views from local or Cloud Storage BigQuery Migration Service (BQMS) translation outputs. Use when provisioning target BigQuery datasets for warehouse migrations, batch loading staged Parquet files into native BigQuery tables by using bq load, auditing loaded table row counts, or deploying already-translated BigQuery views into a target dataset. Don't use for extracting source database catalog metadata, translating SQL queries, views, stored procedures, or DDL schemas to GoogleSQL (use bigquery-migration-sql-translator), exporting or unloading source database tables (such as Snowflake, Databricks, Teradata, or Oracle) to Parquet on Cloud Storage, or running post-migration cross-database data validation.

name: bigquery-migration-metadata-extractor
description: Extracts database catalog metadata and query logs from data warehouses by running the DWH migration extractor locally or on a temporary Google Cloud VM through the BigQuery Migration Cloud Extractor (credentials held in Secret Manager), and inspects extracted `.zip` archives to report object and volume statistics. Use when extracting database metadata or query logs from Snowflake, Redshift, Teradata, Oracle, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Hive, etc., deciding between local and cloud (Cloud Extractor) extraction, or inspecting extracted dwh-migration-*.zip archives to print post-extraction statistics. Don't use for SQL dialect translation (use bigquery-migration-sql-translator), exporting table data to Parquet or CSV files (such as Snowflake `COPY INTO` unloads) or loading it into BigQuery (use the BigQuery Data Transfer Service or bigquery-basics), or validating migrated data.

name: bigquery-migration-sql-translator
description: Translates SQL queries, DDL schemas, and stored procedures from legacy database dialects (Teradata, Oracle, Redshift, Snowflake, SparkSQL, HiveQL) to BigQuery GoogleSQL using the BigQuery Migration Service (BQMS) MCP server. Use when translating legacy SQL queries, migrating schemas or metadata zip archives, or configuring BigQuery Migration Service (BQMS) YAML translation settings. Don't use for executing BigQuery queries or managing datasets and tables (use bigquery-basics), diagnosing runtime job errors (use bigquery-troubleshooting), or tuning slot reservations (use bigquery-optimization).

name: bigquery-migration-validator
description: Validates that tables migrated to BigQuery match their source (Teradata, Snowflake, Oracle, Redshift, Databricks, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MySQL, MariaDB, Hive, Impala, Vertica) with the BigQuery Migration Service (BQMS) validation tool: schema and data type comparison, column aggregate comparison, and row-level data comparison. Use when generating or editing a validation config, running a validation, choosing sampling or partitioning, fixing connection or driver errors, or investigating validation results in BigQuery and Cloud Storage to decide which mismatches to fix. Don't use for SQL translation (use bigquery-migration-sql-translator), extracting source database catalog metadata or query logs, generating SQL scripts (such as COPY INTO) or exporting or unloading source tables to Parquet on Cloud Storage, loading staged files into BigQuery (such as bq load), or general BigQuery query failures and tuning (use bigquery-troubleshooting or bigquery-optimization).

name: bigquery-observability
description: Provides data-retrieval best practices, tool selection guidance, and performant SQL query syntax for BigQuery telemetry across INFORMATION_SCHEMA, Cloud Monitoring, and the REST API. Use when the telemetry to fetch is already known, selecting telemetry tools, writing performant INFORMATION_SCHEMA queries, retrieving telemetry for diagnosing single-job performance bottlenecks, investigating slot contention, job concurrency and queue latency, analyzing reservation capacity, utilization and autoscaling saturation, or auditing capacity-based and on-demand compute and storage resource billable usage. Don't use for root-cause diagnosis or symptom troubleshooting when the cause is unknown (use bigquery-troubleshooting first), or for writing or optimizing business logic SQL (use bigquery-optimization).

name: bigquery-optimization
description: Provides workflows to optimize BigQuery environments (capacity planning, editions), storage assets (partitioning, clustering, storage lifecycles, billing models), and SQL queries. Use when optimizing cost, modeling Edition migrations, rightsizing reservations, evaluating logical vs. physical storage, designing table partitioning/clustering, generating table DDL, migrating unpartitioned tables, managing partition expiration, optimizing individual SQL queries, or evaluating acceleration structures (search indexes, materialized views, BI Engine). Do not use for raw usage reporting (use bigquery-observability), query execution plan analysis, error troubleshooting, or diagnosing why a specific job was slow (use bigquery-troubleshooting).

name: bigquery-troubleshooting
description: Provides diagnostic workflows and step-by-step root-cause analysis procedures for actively broken, failing, or slow BigQuery jobs, execution graph and query plan stage bottlenecks, system performance issues, or unexpectedly expensive workloads. Use when interpreting symptoms, isolating bottlenecks, diagnosing cost spikes (on-demand query spend, capacity slot autoscaling, storage growth), execution graph stages or substep variables, identifying root causes, and determining remediation steps. Don't use for writing or optimizing SQL, proactive capacity planning, or storage layout design (use bigquery-optimization), or when the user already knows which telemetry they want and just needs the query (use bigquery-observability).

name: bigquery-udfs
description: Creates, deploys, and troubleshoots BigQuery User-Defined Functions (UDFs) and Remote Functions across SQL, JavaScript, Python, and Cloud Run endpoints. Use when writing custom scalar or aggregate functions in BigQuery, installing PyPI packages or Cloud Storage libraries in a Python or JavaScript UDF, or calling Google Cloud and external APIs from a Python UDF (WITH CONNECTION) or Remote Function. Don't use for standard BigQuery table/dataset CRUD (use bigquery-basics), DataFrames client workflows (use bigquery-bigframes), or BigQuery ML models (use bigquery-ai-ml).

name: bigtable-basics
description: Assists in provisioning instances/tables, designing performant schemas, and querying data in Bigtable. Use when designing Bigtable row keys, configuring column families, writing SQL queries or client library code (Java, Go, Python) for Bigtable, or diagnosing performance/hotspotting issues. Also use when provisioning Bigtable clusters using gcloud or cbt CLIs. Don't use for generic Cloud SQL administration.

name: cloud-armor-crs-rule-upgrader
description: Upgrades Google Cloud Armor security policies from OWASP CRS 3.0 and 3.3 to OWASP CRS 4.22. Preserves signature opt-in and opt-out lists, translates evaluatePreconfiguredExpr to native evaluatePreconfiguredWaf dictionary parameters, remaps signature IDs to v042200, drops retired signature IDs, and updates structured preconfiguredWafConfig fine-tuning exclusions. Evaluates operational risk (High Breaking Change, Medium Attention Required, Low Clean Upgrade) including Method Enforcement breaking changes (PUT/PATCH/DELETE blocking) and sensitivity coverage expansions. Supports both in-place rule upgrades and smooth preview mode deployments with priority spacing and a 200-rule quota guardrail. Use when a user or agent needs to audit, upgrade, or transition Cloud Armor WAF rules to CRS 4.22. Don't use for non-WAF Cloud Armor rules (IP rate-limiting, geo-blocking, reCAPTCHA) or AWS/Azure WAF migrations.

name: cloud-build-basics
description: Teaches the fundamentals of Cloud Build on Google Cloud. Covers core concepts, API enablement, console navigation to the Build History page, and the end-to-end workflow for creating and manually running a basic build trigger. description: Generates operational guidance for CI/CD deployment pipelines, observability, monitoring, logging, and incident management on Google Cloud based on the design principles and recommendations in the Operational Excellence pillar of the Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework (WAF). Use when the user asks about operations-related topics like capacity management, change management, incident and problem management, configuration management, deployment automation using infrastructure as code (IaC), or operational health checks for Google Cloud workloads.

name: google-cloud-waf-performance-optimization
description: Generates performance-focused guidance for Google Cloud workloads based on the design principles and recommendations in the Performance Optimization pillar of the Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework (WAF). Use this skill to evaluate a workload, identify performance requirements, and provide actionable recommendations for resource allocation, modular design, and elasticity.

name: google-cloud-waf-reliability
description: Evaluates, designs, and improves the reliability, resilience, availability, fault tolerance, and disaster recovery (DR) of Google Cloud workloads based on the design principles and recommendations in the Reliability pillar of the Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework. Use when the user asks about reliability-related topics like workload uptime, designing for high availability (HA) or DR, setting and meeting RTO/RPO targets, SRE best practices, backup strategies, multi-region failover, or fault-tolerant architecture on Google Cloud. Don't use for other Well-Architected Framework pillars such as Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence, or Security, or for hands-on resource deployment and live incident troubleshooting.

name: google-cloud-waf-security
description: Evaluates Google Cloud workloads and provides actionable recommendations for identity management, access control, permissions and roles, network and perimeter security, data security and encryption, security logging and threat detection, software supply chain hardening, AI security, data privacy, regulatory compliance, and cloud sovereignty. The recommendations are aligned with the Security, Privacy, and Compliance pillar of the Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework (WAF). Use when the user asks about firewall rules, zero trust, shared responsibility and shared fate, audit logging, security monitoring, threat mitigation, shift-left CI/CD security, Secure AI Framework (SAIF), data residency, or hardening Google Cloud resources. Don't use for other Well-Architected Framework pillars (Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence, Reliability, Performance Optimization, or Sustainability).

name: google-cloud-waf-sustainability
description: Provides recommendations for environmental sustainability, carbon footprint reduction, and energy efficiency based on the Sustainability pillar of the Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework (WAF). Use when the user asks to assess, design, or optimize Google Cloud workloads for sustainability—including the shared responsibility model, selecting low-carbon regions (CFE%), reducing resource and AI/ML energy waste, designing efficient software and storage lifecycles, or measuring and tracking emissions using Google Cloud Carbon Footprint. Don't use for financial cost reduction (use google-cloud-waf-cost-optimization), latency and throughput tuning (use google-cloud-waf-performance-optimization), or high availability and disaster recovery (use google-cloud-waf-reliability).

name: iam-helper-for-policy-management
description: Streamlines the creation, modification, and management of IAM allow policies (v1) and deny policies (v2). Manages access control across Resource Manager resources (Organization, Folder, Project) and individual resources. Use when creating, updating, listing, or deleting IAM allow policies or deny policies. Don't use for access denial troubleshooting (use iam-helper-for-troubleshooting), temporary privileged access (use iam-helper-for-privileged-access-management), configuring VPC Service Controls, or managing network firewall rules.

name: iam-helper-for-policy-simulator
description: Safely simulates and applies Identity and Access Management (IAM) v1 (Allow) policy changes on Google Cloud. Uses the Policy Simulator to replay historical access logs against proposed policies to prevent breaking active workloads before applying the changes. Use when simulating or applying IAM v1 allow policies across Projects, Folders, or Organizations. Don't use for analyzing IAM v2 deny policies, VPC Service Controls, or performing general policy troubleshooting.

name: iam-helper-for-privileged-access-management
description: Manages the end-to-end lifecycle of on-demand, temporary access using Privileged Access Manager (PAM). Use when a user asks to create, read, update, or delete PAM entitlements, request temporary access, or approve/deny pending PAM grants. Do NOT use for permanent IAM policy bindings, troubleshooting IAM permission errors, or general Google Cloud resource provisioning.

name: iam-helper-for-troubleshooting
description: Diagnoses, remediates, and manages Identity and Access Management (IAM) access issues on Google Cloud. Supports two distinct operational modes: (1) Requester Flow for developers encountering access denials (capturing error context, self-service PAM JIT activations, elevated developer self-remediation, or logging structured tickets), and (2) Resolver Flow for privileged administrators (authoritative Policy Troubleshooter analysis, deny policy exemptions, least-privilege role discovery, and PAM/IAM provisioning).

name: iap-agent-platform-troubleshooting
description: Diagnoses Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) denials of outbound requests from Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform agents that run on Agent Runtime and send traffic through Agent Gateway. Use when an agent request fails with "Egress request is not authorized", when Cloud Audit Logs show an IAP egressViaIAP decision with granted false, when IAP audit entries are missing while debugging agent egress, or when Access policies, IAP allow policies, policy bindings, or Agent Registry entries might block agent egress. Don't use for Gemini model IAM permission errors (such as aiplatform.endpoints.predict), Agent Platform API errors, or Agent Runtime deployment or 500 errors (use agent-platform-troubleshooting instead). Don't use for setting up, creating, or connecting an Agent Gateway, or for IAP web apps, IAP TCP forwarding, or SSH.

name: managed-airflow-dag-authoring
description: Provides guidance for authoring Apache Airflow DAGs in Managed Service for Apache Airflow (MSAA; formerly Cloud Composer). Covers environment context discovery, Airflow 2 vs 3 compatibility, authoring best practices, and local/remote validation processes. Use when creating or extending an Airflow DAG. Don't use when authoring Python code unrelated to Airflow DAGs.

name: managed-airflow-dag-troubleshooting
description: Provides guidance for troubleshooting Apache Airflow DAGs (failed DAG runs and task instances) in Managed Service for Apache Airflow (MSAA; formerly Cloud Composer). Use when figuring out reasons for DAG run or task instance failures. Don't use when looking for overall recommendations for Managed Airflow environment performance.

name: managed-airflow-migrations
description: Provides guidance for migrating Apache Airflow DAGs in Managed Service for Apache Airflow (MSAA; formerly Cloud Composer). Covers migration to Airflow 2.11.1 (MSAA Gen 2 and 3) and Airflow 3 (MSAA Gen 3), including environment inspection, GCS download/upload and scanning patterns for breaking changes. Use when migrating the DAG code to newer Airflow version. Don't use when checking DAG run failures unrelated to code migration.

name: managed-airflow-recommendations
description: Provides recommendations and best practices for creating, configuring, tuning and optimizing Managed Service for Apache Airflow (MSAA; formerly Cloud Composer) environments. Use when the user asks for guidance, recommendations, or best practices on configuring Managed Airflow environments, scaling Airflow environments, preventing workload restarts, or analyzing system health. Don't use for troubleshooting individual DAG or task run failures, authoring DAGs, or migrating DAGs to newer Airflow versions.

name: pathways-workload
description: Debugs failed, crashing or hung Pathways on Cloud workloads (JAX training or inference on Cloud TPU in GKE, run as a JobSet, PathwaysJob or LeaderWorkerSet). Reads Cloud Logging for every Pathways container (user workload, IFRT proxy, pathways-rm, pathways-worker, colocated Python sidecar), node kernel logs and GKE events, then reports the earliest real error, the root cause and a fix. Use when a Pathways workload fails to start, crashes, restarts or stops making progress, or shows errors such as IFRT proxy connection failures, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED lost connection to peer, host OOM kills, ImagePullBackOff, or JAX and Pathways version mismatches. Don't use for GKE workloads that don't use Pathways, or for creating clusters or deploying new Pathways workloads.

name: secops-cases
description: Manage Google Security Operations (SecOps) SOAR cases throughout their lifecycle. Use when listing, creating, inspecting, updating, or closing SOAR cases; adding investigative comments and notes; updating case priority or description; or linking and grouping security alerts within cases. Supports both remote Google SecOps MCP tools and local fallback tools. Don't use for SIEM UDM searches or detection rule authoring.

name: secops-detection-engineering
description: Author, validate, test, and deploy YARA-L 2.0 detection rules and evaluate end-to-end detection coverage gaps in Google SecOps. Use when writing new detection rules, tuning existing rules, validating syntax, testing logic against historical telemetry, or evaluating detection coverage against threat intelligence blogs, CVE disclosures, and Threat Detection Opportunities (TDOs) using synthetic UDM events and long-running coverage analysis. Don't use for alert triage (use secops-triage), deep forensic event reconstruction on infected hosts (use secops-investigate), or case management operations (use secops-cases).

name: secops-hunt
description: Expert guidance for proactive threat hunting in Google SecOps. Use when proactively hunting for threats, retroactively analyzing indicators of compromise (IoCs), performing prevalence searches across enterprise events, hunting for MITRE ATT&CK techniques, or detecting behavioral and statistical outliers using UDM queries. Don't use for incoming alert triage (use secops-triage), active incident response and timeline deep-dives on a known breach (use secops-investigate), or detection rule authoring (use secops-detection-engineering).

name: secops-investigate
description: Expert guidance for deep security incident and entity investigations in Google SecOps. Use when investigating cases, analyzing entities (hosts, IPs, domains, hashes, users), extracting and searching UDM events, performing asset and user timeline analysis, and detecting lateral movement across enterprise networks. Don't use for detection rule authoring or YARA-L tuning (use secops-detection-engineering), proactive hypothesis-driven hunting (use secops-hunt), initial alert triage (use secops-triage), or basic case status updates (use secops-cases).

name: secops-triage
description: Expert guidance for security alert triage in Google SecOps. Use when investigating and triaging security alerts, determining false positives vs. true positives, assessing entity risk, adjusting alert severity or priority, and closing or escalating alerts and cases. Don't use for deep multi-hop incident investigations across host timelines (use secops-investigate), proactive threat hunting or retroactive IoC sweeps (use secops-hunt), or authoring new detection rules (use secops-detection-engineering).

name: spanner-basics
description: Assists in provisioning instances and databases, designing performant schemas, and querying data in Cloud Spanner on Google Cloud. Use when designing primary keys, writing SQL queries or client library code, or diagnosing performance issues.

name: workload-manager-basics
description: Use this skill to manage Google Cloud Workload Manager evaluations, rules, scanned resources, and validation results by using public client libraries and the REST API. Use when you need to inspect workload best-practice rules, create and run evaluations for Google Cloud general best practices, SAP, SQL Server, or custom organizational rules, review violations, export results to BigQuery, or automate Workload Manager through client libraries because no service-specific public CLI or MCP server is available. Don't use for general Google Compute Engine instance management, VPC configuration, or standard IAM auditing.

name: gerrit-code-review
description: Reads and manages Gerrit code reviews over the HTTPS REST API: change metadata and diffs, inline comments and drafts, reviewers and CCs, labels and votes, checks, topics, hashtags, commit messages, cherry-picks, abandon, and submit. Use when working with Android (AOSP), Chromium, Fuchsia, or self-hosted Gerrit, when given a Gerrit change URL (https://*-review.googlesource.com/*, https://r.android.com/*, https://crrev.com/c/*, https://fxrev.dev/*, or https://*/c/*/+/*), or when git commands target a Gerrit host (refs/for/ pushes or branch cherry-picks). Don't use for local-only git operations or GitHub and GitLab pull requests.

name: migrate-to-rust
description: Clones, analyzes, plans, and migrates legacy codebases (C++, Fortran, Java, Python, C, Shell) from a GitHub URL or local directory to a modern, high-performance, deterministic, 100% Safe Rust architecture, tracking live telemetry across every task bucket, test failure/fix cycle, and Profile-Guided Optimization (PGO) stage, and producing a first-person AI storytelling report and interactive HTML infographic. Use when migrating a GitHub repository or local codebase to Rust, porting legacy C++, Fortran, Python, or Java workloads to memory-safe Rust, designing Struct-of-Arrays (SoA) or SIMD Rust architectures, or optimizing Rust ports with LLVM PGO. Don't use for unrelated non-Rust refactoring or single-line syntax questions.

name: dpop-adoption
description: Implement and debug OAuth 2.0 DPoP (RFC 9449) refresh token sender-constraining for WebCrypto, Node.js ES6, and browser runtimes integrating with Google's OAuth platform. Use when configuring non-extractable asymmetric key pairs (P-256), generating DPoP Proof JWTs for authorization code exchange and token refresh, or handling 400 use_dpop_nonce challenge retry loops at oauth2.googleapis.com/token. Don't use for unconstrained OAuth 2.0 flows (where refresh tokens are not bound to a client key pair), or for Google Cloud IAM / service account authentication.

name: sign-in-with-google-web
description: Implement, configure, and secure Sign In With Google (SiwG) using Google Identity Services (GIS / `https://accounts.google.com/gsi/client`) across web architectures. Use when creating Google sign-in buttons, implementing Google One Tap with FedCM, integrating GIS in React/Next.js/Angular/HTML, verifying ID tokens on backend runtimes (Python/Node.js/Go/Java), enforcing Google Workspace domain restrictions (`hd`), securing client-side ID tokens via WebCrypto nonces or encrypted IndexedDB, embedding in cross-origin iframes via the Intermediate Iframe API (`https://accounts.google.com/gsi/intermediate`), configuring Content Security Policy (CSP), COOP, and Permissions Policy (`identity-credentials-get`) headers, or handling sign-out and revocation. Don't use for legacy Google Sign-In (`gapi.auth2`), Google Cloud IAM service accounts, or Android/iOS native Credential Manager.

name: litert-google-tensor
description: Compiles LiteRT (.tflite) models ahead-of-time for Google Tensor TPUs (Tensor G5 on Pixel 10, Tensor G6 on Pixel 11) locally on Linux x86_64 or on Google Colab (--colab on macOS, Windows, or ARM hosts), benchmarks them on a USB-attached Pixel with LiteRT's benchmark_model (NPU latency, peak memory, TPU tile time, TPU energy, optional CPU baseline), and packages compiled models for an Android Gradle app as a Google Play AI pack with the Tensor NPU runtime module and a Kotlin loader, applies it to the app and verifies it on a Pixel. Use when the user asks to compile, AOT-compile, or prepare a .tflite model for the Pixel TPU/NPU, check whether a .tflite is already Tensor-compiled, measure on-device NPU performance of a compiled model, or package or deploy a compiled model into their Android app (or replace the one it ships). Don't use for Qualcomm, MediaTek, or Samsung NPUs, GPU-only benchmarking, LiteRT-LM or LLM (.litertlm) models, on-device JIT compilation, non-Gradle builds, or publishing to Google Play.

name: <slug>
description: <What it does and when to use it, in one or two sentences. This is what an agent matches on. At most 1,024 characters.>

name: learn-my-brand
description: Learn my brand once and stop asking me every time. Use when someone says learn my brand, set up my brand, here's our brand book, remember how we talk, what can we claim, can we say this, approve our claims, sign off our voice, our price or product changed, the client approved the claims, pick up where we left off, or check our claims are still current. Reads what GooseWorks already found about the brand, asks only the gaps as drafts to confirm, audits every claim (including ones research marked approved) and gets the ones that matter signed off with proof, scope and review date, turns the voice into rules the owner confirms, checks logo, colours and fonts, and saves it all as it goes so every other job loads it instead of asking. Ends with an unknowns list and a read-back. Not for who our customers are and what they say (use research-audience) or writing positioning from scratch (not covered yet).

name: make-product-photos
description: Use when the marketer says: studio photos of my product without a shoot, product photos for my store page, packshots on white, lifestyle or on-model shots, photos for the new colourway, fresh product imagery for ads, photos for our launch page, our packaging changed — redo the photos, I have no photographer. Delivers store-ready product photos generated from the brand's real product photos: a shot list built from the page slots (hero, alt angle, scale, detail, in use, lifestyle, on-model), only real photos of this product as references, matched to the brand's photography, every shot checked against the real product for shape, parts, logo, text, colour, finish, scale and honest representation, with a keep / maybe / reject verdict and a page order. The human picks the keepers. Never uploads to a store, never shows a size, part, feature or result the product lacks. Not for ads with text, infographics or screenshots — make-static-ads; not for marketplace listing sets (not covered yet).

name: make-video-ads
description: Use when the marketer says: make me a video ad, a 30-second ad for paid social, a Reel / TikTok / Shorts ad, a UGC-style video made with AI (no real creator), a product demo video, remake this ad I like for my brand, cut our best organic video into an ad, more like my winning video with new hooks, my video ad got rejected — fix it. Delivers a produced, ready-to-post video ad grounded in a researched angle: one message, a hook for the first two seconds, every claim traced to the brand's signed-off claims, no generated person posing as a customer, the exact words and the price approved before anything renders (one video, or one plus two hook variants), an honest review of the result, priced fixes only on a yes, and launch copy and notes for the ads team. Works in chat apps. Never publishes or spends ad budget. Not for real creators filming for you — work-with-creators (unsure? ask: AI-made or a real person); not for a phone-shot organic post — run-organic-social; not for static ads — make-static-ads.

name: goose-ads
description: Edit, resize, animate and study image ads with GooseWorks in this chat. New static or image ads go to the make-static-ads skill when it is installed or catalog_fetch opens it. Read the brand and follow the active playbook, preserving factual prerequisites and approvals.

name: goose-product-photos
description: Make product photos (studio, lifestyle or on a model) of a brand's real products with GooseWorks in this chat. Start brand work with brand_knowledge_browse and follow the next_step in every answer.

name: goose-video
description: Make a video ad in this chat from a real reference ad, found or theirs; styles are the fallback. Follow every answer's next_step.

name: goose-video-local
description: Make an approved GooseWorks video when an answer's next_step gives its command.

name: gooseworks
description: GooseWorks growth coworker and router for markets, competitors, audiences, creators, campaigns, ads, photos, graphics, video, content, email, SEO, social, leads and contacts. Use for brand facts or copy too, so offers, prices, rules, audience and bestsellers reach the brand's Marketing Brain.

name: make-custom-video
description: Create a custom video with sourced product accuracy, explicit sound routing and exact-final audiovisual review.

name: ad-policy-check
description: Checks paid ads against the ad platform's rules (Meta, TikTok, Google, LinkedIn and others) and the brand's category rules: the copy, on-image or on-screen text, pictures and people. Rewrites what can be fixed honestly, adds the disclosures that are needed, and flags anything that needs a human or legal review, with one pass, fixed or flag line per ad and platform. Use alone when you already have the ad text or images and know where they will run; otherwise run the playbook for the job (e.g. make-static-ads, make-content, email-lifecycle).

name: analyze-performance
description: Weekly performance read across every channel we run: what worked, why, and what to make next, judged on the business's real number (store revenue, qualified pipeline, retained users), not platform claims. Use when: write my Monday report; how are my ads doing — which ad won?; are my ads actually making money (Meta says 4x ROAS but revenue is flat); why did sales drop this week; did the test win; is my tracking working; monthly numbers for the replan; anything on fire today. Not for acting on the recommendations (pausing, scaling, launching) — use run-paid-campaigns; not for replanning the budget — use plan-campaign.

name: analyze-performance-call-and-learn
description: Step of the analyze-performance playbook: calls ended tests, scores last week's calls, writes this week's kill/scale/hold calls and drafts learnings for the brand brain. Run analyze-performance instead; not for direct use.

name: analyze-performance-diagnose
description: Step of the analyze-performance playbook: flags tracking breaks with fixes and explains each big metric move with evidence, confidence and ruled-out causes. Run analyze-performance instead; not for direct use.

name: analyze-performance-intake
description: Step of the analyze-performance playbook: gathers the week's numbers from tools, exports and pastes, cleans them, and writes the coverage line or switches to claims-only mode. Run analyze-performance instead; not for direct use.

name: analyze-performance-rank-and-read
description: Step of the analyze-performance playbook: ranks creative by angle, hook and format with spend gates, writes short per-channel reads and drafts what to make next. Run analyze-performance instead; not for direct use.

name: analyze-performance-revenue-join
description: Step of the analyze-performance playbook: joins cleaned store or CRM numbers with ad spend to build the business-truth table, MER, new-customer cost and the overclaim ratio. Run analyze-performance instead; not for direct use.

name: claims-gate
description: Checks every claim in a piece of copy (ads, emails, posts, pages, scripts, briefs) against the claims the brand has approved. Keeps, rewrites or cuts each line, and lists the proof that would bring a cut line back. When a line the copy needs has no approval, it asks for a short sign-off on the 3 or 4 lines that matter and records the answer. Use alone when you already have the copy and a brand set up; otherwise run the playbook for the job (e.g. make-static-ads, make-content, write-outreach).

name: email-lifecycle
description: Lifecycle email, SMS and push: audits the list and deliverability, then writes the flows this kind of business needs first, loadable as-is in your own tool, plus segments, cadence and this week's broadcasts. Never sends anything. Use when: set up my welcome and abandoned-cart emails; trial onboarding or waitlist launch emails; win back lapsed customers; plan this week's emails and texts; push notifications for my app; why are my emails going to spam; plan our Black Friday email and SMS sends; a send went wrong. Not for cold outreach to prospects — use write-outreach; not the editorial newsletter issue — use make-content; not the whole cross-channel Black Friday plan — use plan-campaign.

name: email-lifecycle-broadcast-planner
description: Step of the email-lifecycle playbook: builds the month's send calendar and writes this week's email and SMS broadcasts against the approved cadence and segments. Run email-lifecycle instead; not for direct use.

name: email-lifecycle-flow-writer
description: Step of the email-lifecycle playbook: writes one lifecycle flow as a build sheet for the brand's email tool, every message finished in the brand voice. Run email-lifecycle instead; not for direct use.

name: email-lifecycle-lifecycle-audit
description: Step of the email-lifecycle playbook: audits list, consent, live flows, recent sends and sending setup, marking every item verified, from-you or unknown. Run email-lifecycle instead; not for direct use.

name: email-lifecycle-offer-math
description: Prices one discount, free-shipping threshold or referral reward against contribution margin: cost per order, share of margin used, break-even lift, code leakage risks, and one recommended offer in two plain sentences. Use alone when you already have the offer, average order value and margin per product; otherwise run email-lifecycle.

name: email-lifecycle-send-check
description: Checks a drafted email flow or broadcast before it is loaded: flow logic and exits, overlaps, offer depth and codes, stock, claims, consent and legal footer, SMS rules, rendering, voice and AI-copy tells, and the goal metric. Returns a pass / fixed / open-question table. Use alone when you already have the finished draft and the brand's product and policy facts; otherwise run email-lifecycle.

name: honest-review
description: Shared step of the marketing playbooks (make-static-ads, run-organic-social): how to review generated images and video honestly. Covers what was seen by eye versus read automatically, findings framed as things for the human to confirm, remakes only after a yes to the price, and at most two tries per item. Loaded by those playbooks; not for direct use.

name: improve-search-visibility
description: SEO and AI-answer visibility. Use for a site SEO or technical audit with ranked fixes, competitor keyword and topic gaps, a topic cluster, SEO metrics for domains, a programmatic SEO page-set plan, or checking where ChatGPT and Google name the brand. Delivers the requested audit, comparison, map or blueprint with dated evidence and clear data limits. Also covers app store listings and local search. Drafts changes; never edits live. Full pages go to make-content; paid search goes to run-paid-campaigns.

name: improve-search-visibility-citation-check
description: Step of the improve-search-visibility playbook: runs the agreed buyer questions on AI and Google surfaces, records every run and scores how often the brand is named. Run improve-search-visibility instead; not for direct use.

name: improve-search-visibility-entity-footprint
description: Step of the improve-search-visibility playbook: checks the profiles answer engines read, plus local listings and reviews, against the brand's facts and writes corrections. Run improve-search-visibility instead; not for direct use.

name: improve-search-visibility-fix-writer
description: Step of the improve-search-visibility playbook: turns one ranked fix into paste-ready site copy or code with owner, risk and undo, and writes page briefs. Run improve-search-visibility instead; not for direct use.

name: improve-search-visibility-page-and-foundation-check
description: Step of the improve-search-visibility playbook: audits site indexing, crawling, technical and page issues at the requested scope, or checks pages behind lost visibility questions. Run improve-search-visibility instead; not for direct use.

name: improve-search-visibility-question-set
description: Step of the improve-search-visibility playbook: drafts and scores the buyer-question set in AI and Google forms and groups it into page clusters. Run improve-search-visibility instead; not for direct use.

name: improve-search-visibility-store-listing-audit
description: Audits an app's App Store and Google Play listing against three competitors (title, subtitle, description opening, first screenshots and captions, rating, review themes) and writes a field-by-field rewrite with character counts, or a launch-day listing before release. Use alone when you already have the app's store links and signed-off product facts; otherwise run improve-search-visibility.

name: make-content
description: Writes marketing content: articles, single posts, newsletters, scripts and repurposed cuts, each with an edit note and a claims check. Use when a marketer says "write a blog post / case study", "write a LinkedIn or X post / thread / X article", "carousel copy", "draft this week's newsletter", "turn this webinar into posts" or "repurpose this", "write a TikTok or YouTube script", "refresh this old post", or "write the page from this SEO brief". Words only; nothing is invented or published. Not for a dated posting calendar — use run-organic-social; not ad copy (make-static-ads) or promo emails (email-lifecycle). Press releases, landing and product pages, and sales decks are not covered.

name: make-content-content-brief
description: Writes a one-page content brief before any draft: audience, intent, the one arguable point, what top results already say and what this piece adds, an outline, a proof inventory with gaps marked, voice, CTA and banned words, checked against six gates. Use alone when you already have the topic, format, audience and destination and want only the brief; otherwise run make-content.

name: make-content-source-to-units
description: Step of the make-content playbook: mines one finished asset into scored quotable units and maps a different lead unit to each platform. Run make-content instead; not for direct use.

name: make-content-two-pass-edit
description: Edits an existing draft in order: a substance pass (arguable thesis, swap test, fakes removed, CTA fit), a claims and fact check that cuts or softens unproven lines, a readability and voice-match pass, then an AI-tell sweep, with an edit note listing open gaps. Use alone when you already have a finished draft and the brand's voice samples and approved claims; otherwise run make-content.

name: make-static-ads
description: Make new static image ads, a fresh batch, more ads, a winner's variations, copy variants or a rejected ad fix. Reads the brand, its customers and the ads it already runs, turns real product facts and customer situations into distinct visual ideas, shows a concept board, writes each render prompt, quotes, renders and reviews through GooseWorks. Also handles requested branded header/social graphics. Use for static ad creation rather than goose-ads. Not for video, product photos or launching campaigns.

name: make-static-ads-ad-copy
description: Step of make-static-ads: writes the text for each slot the ad's template sets, then the primary texts, headline, description and CTA around the image, from usable facts and customer words. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.

name: make-static-ads-claims-extract
description: Step of the make-static-ads playbook: pulls every claim-bearing span out of an ad — the copy around the image, the on-image words in the prompt, badges, and what the picture implies — and keeps or cuts each by the brand-brain rule. Runs before spend on the finished prompt (Pass A) and on every render (Pass B). Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.

name: make-static-ads-compose
description: Step of make-static-ads: writes each ad's render prompt and ordered image list from its concept-board row, one per ad and ratio, ready for a quoted render. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.

name: make-static-ads-concept-grid
description: Step of make-static-ads: turns the chosen angles into messages, visual ideas and a template per ad, checks each against the brand profile and recent ads, writes the concept board and has a fresh critic attack it before any copy, prompt or spend. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.

name: make-static-ads-copy-variants
description: Step of the make-static-ads playbook: after an image is approved, makes more versions of the same picture with different hooks, headlines or fonts by a quoted re-render with the approved render attached as the brand's own image, so copy can be tested without new visuals. Offered, never default. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.

name: make-static-ads-find-references
description: Step of make-static-ads: picks a template for every ad in its chosen style, after its visual idea and style are set, from the brand's own ads, the GooseWorks library or category leaders, and records what the chosen creativity level keeps from it. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.

name: make-static-ads-fix-rejected
description: Step of the make-static-ads playbook: fixes a static image ad the platform rejected — finds the ad, maps the platform's reason to the line or element at fault, fixes copy for free or re-composes the image text on a quote, re-runs the claims and policy checks, and answers the request. A rejected video is the video playbook's job. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.

name: make-static-ads-graphic-request
description: Makes one simple non-ad brand graphic, such as an email header, social feed or story image, or a blog or link-preview image, in the brand's style with at most a short line of text, after claim and rights checks and a yes to the quote; returns the link and alt text. Not for carousels, decks or print. Use alone when you already have the purpose, placement and exact wording; otherwise run make-static-ads.

name: make-static-ads-render-review
description: Step of make-static-ads: a fresh judge checks every render against its concept-board row and the official product photos, one retry inside the marketer's approval, then the claims and set checks; records each verdict in tags and the batch file. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.

name: marketing-data-access
description: How to get live public data (ads libraries, social posts and comments, search results, creator profiles), business identity/work-contact reads, domain SEO metrics and paid media generation through GooseWorks, with no vendor key. Load before any playbook step that reads public data or calls an outside model: which proxy call fits the job, what it costs, how to get the human's yes, and what to do when the data is not reachable. Not for brand facts (read the brand brain) or the customer's own ad accounts (the GooseWorks ads tools, or an ads connector they have).

name: marketing-guide
description: How every GooseWorks marketing playbook runs: connecting, picking the brand, where files go, the shared claims, money, research and schedule rules, and the index of what each playbook saves and who reads it. Load at the start of any playbook run. Not a marketer ask: for "what should I do first?" use where-to-start.

name: outcomes-ledger
description: Shared step of the marketing playbooks (research-audience, write-outreach, work-with-creators): keeps the brand's record of the prospects or creators that were handed over. Tracks a status for each person, permanent opt-outs, re-check dates and dated lessons, which the next run reads. Loaded by those playbooks; not for direct use.

name: plan-campaign
description: Campaign planner: turns a product, offer, goal, budget and date into a plan the marketer can approve and a designer can start from today, with every channel kept or dropped for a reason. Zero paid is a valid answer; it never spends. Use when the ask names a campaign, a launch, drop or season push, a budget or a date: I have this budget and a launch date — what do I run, where?; plan my launch, drop or Black Friday push; plan a campaign; how should I split $5k; plan next month's campaign; our CAC blew up — replan. Not for a broad "grow my brand", "get more customers" or "where do I start" with no campaign, budget or date — use where-to-start; not for pausing ads on a sold-out product — use run-paid-campaigns; not for an email-only send plan — use email-lifecycle; not for reading this week's numbers — use analyze-performance.

name: plan-campaign-brief-and-assets
description: Step of the plan-campaign playbook: writes angles per channel, the asset list, measurement plan, hand-offs and replan triggers, then assembles the plan. Run plan-campaign instead; not for direct use.

name: plan-campaign-budget-and-tests
description: Step of the plan-campaign playbook: splits the budget across chosen channels, checks per-channel minimums, and writes the test plan and paid structure. Run plan-campaign instead; not for direct use.

name: plan-campaign-channel-decision
description: Step of the plan-campaign playbook: marks each candidate channel Run, Test, Later or No with a brand-fact reason and founder hours. Run plan-campaign instead; not for direct use.

name: plan-campaign-goal-chain
description: Checks whether a stated goal is reachable on a given budget: fills an economics box with a source on every number, subtracts the baseline, works out the implied cost per customer against history or labelled base rates, and flags when the goal needs renegotiating. Use alone when you already have the goal (metric, number, date), budget, order value, margin and baseline; otherwise run plan-campaign.

name: research-audience
description: Audience research: who the buyers are, in their own words, where they gather and how to reach them — plus named prospect lists when asked. Use when the marketer says "research our audience", "who should we target", "mine our reviews", "why do people buy us or leave", "where does our audience hang out"; or for lists: "find 50 right-fit leads with emails", "find retailers or accounts to pitch", "score these leads / who do we call first", "who's looking for an alternative to X", "tell me when a past champion changes jobs". Reads the brand's own customer data first and delivers a readable report saved to the brand. Never contacts anyone. Not for market size or trends — use research-market; not for writing the messages — use write-outreach.

name: research-audience-account-sourcing
description: Step of the research-audience playbook: finds candidate accounts matching the fit definition, confirms gates, applies exclusions and dedupes. Run research-audience instead; not for direct use.

name: research-audience-fit-definition
description: Step of the research-audience playbook: drafts the searchable fit definition, exclusions and list size that the list run then searches on. Run research-audience instead; not for direct use.

name: research-audience-people-and-contacts
description: For a list of companies, picks 1-3 current people per company in different buying roles, confirms each title with a dated source, finds a public contact route, labels email status honestly and flags regions with contact rules. Never contacts anyone. Use alone when you already have a vetted company list and the buyer titles; otherwise run research-audience.

name: research-audience-score-segment-qa
description: Step of the research-audience playbook: scores and tiers list rows, groups them into segments with an angle each, runs the pre-handover checks and writes the list files. Run research-audience instead; not for direct use.

name: research-audience-segment-pass
description: Step of the research-audience playbook: the worker brief for researching one buyer group, returning notes in a fixed shape. Run research-audience instead; not for direct use.

name: research-audience-signals-and-hooks
description: For a list of companies, finds dated, linked timing signals from the last 90 days (funding, new leaders, hiring, launches), drops stale ones and noise, scores timing, and gives one personal hook per person from their recent public work. Facts only, no message copy. Use alone when you already have the company list and, for hooks, the people; otherwise run research-audience.

name: research-competitors
description: Competitor research: what every main rival is running, launching, charging and saying now, what works for them, and what that means for you. Use when the marketer asks for competitor research or a teardown, "what ads are my competitors running", "how do they price", "find gaps and angles", "what changed this week" (a weekly watch), or "X just launched / shut down / cut prices" (react now). Also builds a sales battlecard, checks a competitor page's tools/pixels, or studies who engages with their LinkedIn posts. Delivers a readable report saved to the brand, so the next run reports what changed. Never copies their words or disparages them. Not for what people say about you or your market — use research-market; not for who your buyers are — use research-audience.

name: research-competitors-category-pass
description: Step of the research-competitors playbook: the worker brief covering the whole category, including searches, AI answers, community threads and category ad winners. Run research-competitors instead; not for direct use.

name: research-competitors-edge-cases
description: Step of the research-competitors playbook: rules for run edge cases such as no browser, stalled workers, earlier reports and late reads. Run research-competitors instead; not for direct use.

name: research-competitors-rival-pass
description: Step of the research-competitors playbook: the worker brief for profiling one rival at a capped depth, returning a fixed-shape profile. Run research-competitors instead; not for direct use.

name: research-market
description: Market research and brand watch: which market the brand is in, how big the reachable part is, what's changing, how buyers buy and what they pay, what people are saying now, and what it means for positioning. Use when the marketer asks for market research, "how big is my market", "what's changing in my category", "what do others charge", "what are people saying about us", "is there demand for <idea>", or "watch my brand / tell me if something blows up" (alerts only, risk first). Also writes positioning choices and finished messages ("position my product", "write our positioning"). Researches first, asks only decisions at the end, and saves the output to the brand. Not for who the buyers are and their own words — use research-audience; not for a deep look at rivals — use research-competitors.

name: research-market-edge-cases
description: Step of the research-market playbook: rules for run edge cases such as no browser, stalled workers, earlier reports and late reads. Run research-market instead; not for direct use.

name: research-market-listening
description: Step of the research-market playbook: the worker brief for listening to what people say about the brand and category, risks first. Run research-market instead; not for direct use.

name: research-market-market-pass
description: Step of the research-market playbook: the worker brief for researching the market itself, including category, size, changes, pricing norms and demand. Run research-market instead; not for direct use.

name: run-memory
description: Shared step of the marketing playbooks (analyze-performance, run-paid-campaigns, research-competitors, email-lifecycle): reads the last run's record, checks whether its recommendations were done and whether they worked, and saves a short record of this run for the next one. Loaded by those playbooks; not for direct use.

name: run-organic-social
description: Runs a brand's organic social: how each platform works now, a strategy per platform and two weeks of posts in the brand's or a person's real voice. Use when a marketer says "run organic social for my brand", "fill my social calendar", "plan two weeks of posts", "grow my X / LinkedIn / Instagram / TikTok", "ghostwrite my founder's posts", "which platforms should we be on?", "plan the social for our launch", "a TikTok or Reel script to shoot on my phone", "tear down @x's account", or "my accounts went quiet".
